ba-don-lockwood.description: A chocolate, smoky riff on the old fashioned that proves simple variations on classic cocktails can have impressive results. This is one of my favourite modern classic cocktails featured in New York Cocktails published by Cider Mill Press.

ingredients.name: Falernum
ingredients.note: preferably John D Taylor's Velvet Falernum

ba-dons-mai-tai.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Dump into a double rocks glass and top with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a brandied cherry, lime wedge and mint bouquet.
ba-dons-mai-tai.description: Don’s Mai Tai is a tiki cocktail recipe originally from Don the Beachcomber. The tropical drink combines rum, absinthe, grapefruit and more.
ba-dons-mai-tai.garnish: brandied cherry, lime wedge, fresh mint

ba-doubleplusgood.method_text: Dry-shake all ingredients (except the bitters) first without ice, then again with ice added. Double-strain through a fine mesh strainer into a chilled short glass, no ice. Drop the bitters atop the foam in the shape of two plus symbols.
ba-doubleplusgood.description:
Doubleplusgood is Boston barman John Gertsen’s take on a Mai Tai, crossed with a Pisco Sour. It’s mildly sweet, with the gentle almond flavor of orgeat laced through the delicate foam of egg white (or aquafaba, if you prefer).

The garnish is a signature of Gertsen’s recipe: two plus signs, drawn in the foam with aromatic bitters.
ba-doubleplusgood.garnish: two plus signs, drawn in the foam with aromatic bitters

ba-dreamy-dorini-smoking-martini.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a cocktail glass.
3. Express the oils from the lemon twist over the drink, then garnish with the twist.
ba-dreamy-dorini-smoking-martini.description: This Vodka Martini riff from Audrey Saunders is anything but ordinary, with peaty single malt scotch and Pernod taking the place of dry vermouth and orange bitters.

ba-drifter.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir gently.
2. Strain into a double rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with a grapefruit twist.
ba-drifter.description: At ABV in San Francisco, the concept is simple: The menu is built around the spirits that the owners want to drink, and the drinks they want to make from them. This cocktail, the Drifter, is a straightforward mixture of Japanese whisky, blanc vermouth, Amaro Nonino and Peychaud’s bitters, garnished with a grapefruit twist.

ba-drunk-uncle.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir for 30-45 sec. or approx. 60 revolutions.
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-drunk-uncle.description:
Drunk Uncle is a cocktail inspired by a negroni, specifically a scotch negroni, with bold, strong bitter-sweet and boozy taste profile. Although in my mind it has left the true negroni specs in order to explore a more inventive and just as delicious direction.

As you probably guessed base spirit of this cocktail is a scotch, in this particular case smoky and funky Islay scotch takes the centre stage. It is then paired with Cynar, a bitter-sweet artichoke liqueur with deep flavours balanced by the subtle vegetal and herbal notes. For me it plays incredibly well with Islay scotch, probably even better than Campari would. Addition of bianco vermouth brings a touch more sweetness and delicate herbaceousness to the mix binding the cocktail into a delicious whole. Last, but not least, grapefruit peel serves not only as an eye-catching garnish, but also expands the aromatic dimension of the cocktail, giving it a light, fresh citrusy touch.

All in all, Drunk Uncle is my kind of negroni, dark, bold and full of amazing flavour. I might be partial here, since I love Cynar, but for me there is no better negroni variation for these cold and dark winter evenings.
ba-drunk-uncle.garnish: Garnish with a twist of grapefruit.

ingredients.name: Gin
ingredients.note: New York Distilling Co.’ Dorothy Parker

ingredients.name: Navy Strength Gin
ingredients.note: New York Distilling Co. Perry’s Tot

ba-e-tonico.method_text:
1. Combine the first five ingredients in a Collins glass and fill with ice.
2. Top with tonic water.
3. Garnish with a bay leaf.
ba-e-tonico.description: E Tonico is a Gin & Tonic with an Italian twist courtesy of an aperitivo liqueur, vermouth and saline solution.

ba-eastside.method_text:
1. Add three cucumbers slices and mint leaves to a shaker.
2. Muddle gently for 5-7 seconds.
3. Add gin, lime juice, simple syrup, and cubed ice to shaker.
4. Shake for 10-20 seconds.
5. Fine strain into a cocktail glass.
ba-eastside.description: The Eastside is a gin-based cocktail recipe that was created by George Delgado at Libation in New York City, New York. This variation was adapted from the book Steve The Bartender's Cocktail Guide by Steve Roennfeldt.
ba-eastside.garnish: Garnish with remaining cucumber slice and mint sprig.

ba-eel-bars-marianito.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice, then garnish with an olive on a pick and an orange twist.
ba-eel-bars-marianito.description: This Marianito cocktail recipe swaps the typical gin for rum, specifically an agricole rhum. It's a low-proof, Negroni-like drink.

ba-eeyores-requiem.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
3. Express three orange twists over the surface of the drink, discarding the first two and saving the third for garnish.
ba-eeyores-requiem.description: Three bitter amari, including Fernet-Branca, get amped up with aromatic French vermouth and juniper-rich gin in this cocktail recipe.

ba-eggnog.method_text:
1. Separate the eggs.
2. Whisk the yolks and sugar together until they firm up and their bright orange color fades to a more opaque pale yellow.
3. Slowly add the spirits, milk and cream while continuing to whisk air into the batch.
4. Beat the egg whites and salt together to stiff peaks.
5. Whisk the egg whites into the mixture.
6. Bottle and store in the refrigerator until chilled, the longer the better.
7. When ready to serve, pour into a chilled Nick & Nora glass and top with freshly grated nutmeg.
ba-eggnog.description: An archetypal example of a traditional eggnog recipe with farm-fresh dairy and a blend of whiskey, rum and Cognac.

ingredients.name: Amaro
ingredients.note: Trino uses Maxico Mistico Licor del Sobador

ba-el-abuelo.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir for approximately 10 seconds.
2. Strain over a large ice cube into the glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-el-abuelo.description: This Old Fashioned-inspired cocktail by Carolina González of Chicago's Trino adds warmth and depth to the whiskey cocktail using the earthy herbaceousness of a Mexican amaro and the baking spices of a spiced brown nectar. "It’s the kind of drink you want when it’s cold out, sitting by a fire, or winding down after dinner," says González.
ba-el-abuelo.garnish: Sprig of thyme and an orange swath

ba-el-gibson.method_text:
1. Place the pickled onion wedge in a chilled Nick & Nora glass. In a mixing glass, stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into the prepared glass.
2. Pickled Spring OnionsThoroughly wash a bunch of spring onions, and use a knife to remove all of the green parts. Cut the onions into wedges, maintaining the root end (to hold the onion together). Pack the onions into a sanitized canning jar or a large food-safe plastic storage container.
3. In a pot, combine a mixture of 60 percent water and 40 percent champagne vinegar (the quantity will depend on the size of the batch you’re preparing). Weigh this liquid mixture and add 5 percent of its weight in sugar, and 3 percent of its weight in salt. Add several bay leaves, 1 Tbsp. of black peppercorns, and 1 Tbsp. of coriander seeds, and bring the mixture to a boil, whisking to dissolve the sugar.
4. Once the mixture is boiling, remove it from the heat and pour it over the onions, to cover. Cover the container and let it cool; will keep refrigerated for up to 1 month.
ba-el-gibson.description: "In the spring, we went hard on spring onions at the farmers market, and pickled them,” says John Douglass of Imbibe 75 Place to Watch, Pretty Decent in Louisville, Kentucky. “The brine became the dirty in this Gibson riff from our second menu.” Douglass notes that if spring onions aren’t in season, the recipe still works perfectly well using small yellow onions.

ba-el-pepe.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over a large rock into a rocks glass.
4. Garnish with a basil leaf.
ba-el-pepe.description: Although A16’s El Pepe cocktail recipe looks innocent in a glass, it’s delightfully complex, built with a structure similar to Margarita.

ba-el-presidente.method_text: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
ba-el-presidente.description: The El Presidente earned its acclaim in Havana during the 1920s through the 1940s during the American Prohibition. It quickly became the preferred drink of the Cuban upper class.

ba-elder-fashion-gin.method_text: Stir everything with ice, strain to glass.

ba-electric-current-fizz.method_text:
1. In a shaker, combine all ingredients except for soda water. Add one small piece of ice and shake until the ice is dissolved; this helps emulsify the egg white.
2. Add more ice to the shaker and hard shake, then strain into a fizz glass or short Collins glass.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Serve the fizz with the prairie oyster in a shot glass.

### Prairie Oyster

Reserve the egg yolk, taking care not to puncture it. Season the yolk with a pinch of salt, black pepper and Worcestershire sauce and Tabasco to taste (start with one dash of each). Serve in a shot glass alongside the drink.


Note: The appeal of the Prairie Oyster lies in the seasoned yolk bursting during the shot, so take care not to puncture it.
ba-electric-current-fizz.description: The Electric Current Fizz is an easy cocktail recipe that pairs a gin fizz with a prairie oyster, a dressed egg yolk shot.
ba-electric-current-fizz.garnish: Prairie Oyster in a shot glass

ba-employees-onlys-mezcal-margarita.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker, and add ice.
2. Shake until chilled and strain into ice-filled tumbler glass.
ba-employees-onlys-mezcal-margarita.description:
Steve Schneider, principal bartender at New York’s Employees Only, has a long history with Margaritas. “I love Margaritas, I always have,” he says. “The Margarita has been a progression of my career, because in my 13 years behind the bar, it’s been the drink I’ve always had to make, even if it was in a shitty dive bar, with 18 beers on tap, making disco drinks.”

Now, the mezcal-spiked version is a regular after-hours feature at EO, where the rest of the staff shares his love of the classic.

ba-endless-summer.method_text:
1. In a large shaking tin, add all ingredients. Add ice, and shake well.
2. Fine strain into a Collins glass over ice.


 ## Editors note:

This drink can easily be scaled up into a large-format cocktail; for guidelines, see <a href="https://punchdrink.com/articles/five-batched-summer-cocktails-recipes/">here</a>.
ba-endless-summer.description: Yanni Kehagiaras riffs on the Negroni cocktail recipe with Campari, gin, sweet vermouth, and an ounce of pineapple.

ba-english-garden.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Strain over fresh ice into a high ball
ba-english-garden.description: The English Garden brings together some classic pairings for St-Germain Elderflower liqueur - gin, apple, lime & cucumber. Served long, this one is filled with quintessential English flavours.

ba-enzo.method_text:
1. Add the first three ingredients to a Collins or highball glass over ice.
2. Top with soda water and garnish with an orange peel or a half-slice.
ba-enzo.description: The Enzo is an Americano cocktail made with a Ferrari, the 50/50 shot of fernet amaro and Campari. Here’s the easy aperitivo recipe.

ba-enzoni.method_text: Muddle grapes, add ingredients, shake then double strain. Garnish with more green grapes on a cocktail pick.
ba-enzoni.description: The Enzoni Cocktail is a true modern classic that will impress your guests! This gin-based drink is perfect for any occasion and is a fun and delicious take on some of your favorite classic cocktails!

ba-eponine-collins.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a collins glass over ice and top with soda.
3. Garnish with two cucumber slices and two basil leaves.
ba-eponine-collins.description: A French-inflected Collins cocktail recipe from Sarah Morrissey builds on a base of gin, complemented by Suze and Amaro Montenegro.

ba-eric-alperins-tuxedo-no-2.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients, except absinthe, in a mixing glass over cracked ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe rinsed or atomized with absinthe.
3. Express lemon twist, then use as garnish. Finish off with a brandied cherry.
ba-eric-alperins-tuxedo-no-2.description: This variation on the Tuxedo cocktail recipe—a sherry-spiked Martini—dates to the turn of the 20th century and swaps sherry for dry vermouth.

ba-fairy-sugar-momma.description: As much as I liked the hint of anise in a corpse reviver I never was one to eat a black jelly bean on its own. But I think this drink works so well because all of the ingredients it’s brought together with are also bold and don't allow the absinthe to dominate the drink. It’s black jelly bean on a tropical vacation and it is tasty.

ingredients.name: Bourbon Whiskey
ingredients.note: preferably Elijah Craig Small Batch or Old Forester

ba-fancy-free.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled double rocks glass over a big cube.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.
ba-fancy-free.description: The Fancy Free is a variation on the Old-Fashioned. This cocktail recipe combines bourbon whiskey, maraschino liqueur and bitters.

ba-femme-fatale.method_text:
1. Pour the sparkling wine into a chilled coupe. Shake the remaining ingredients and fine strain into the coupe. Optional: Shake hibiscus dust on the surface of the cocktail and swirl with a barspoon.
Passion Fruit Vanilla SyrupIf using frozen purée, thaw 2 1/4 oz. of passion fruit purée (Long Goodbye uses Perfect Purée) completely and bring to room temperature. Add 2 1/4 oz. of granulated sugar and 1/3 tsp. of vanilla syrup and whisk to combine completely. Refrigerate to store. Makes approximately 6 servings and will keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Hibiscus DustUsing a spice grinder, pulse 1/4 cup of dried hibiscus flowers to a fine powder. Store in a shaker. Makes approximately 6 servings.
ba-femme-fatale.description: Rather than serving sparkling wine alongside their Pornstar Martini variation, Austin's The Long Goodbye adds it directly to the glass. "A vanilla infusion lends to a drier finish than the traditional addition of vanilla-flavored liqueur, with the passion fruit providing a citrusy, floral, and melon-forward brightness highlighted by the toasty cremant," says Seth Odland, bar lead and beverage director.

ba-ferrari.method_text: 1. Combine and drink as a shot.
ba-ferrari.description: The Ferrari cocktail recipe, a potent 50/50 split of Fernet-Branca and Campari, can be taken as a shot or sipped slowly.

ba-final-ward.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass
ba-final-ward.description:
The Final Ward is perhaps the best-know riff on the classic Last Word and was created in 2007 by Phil Ward at Death & Co. NYC. It is still comprised of equal parts with rye whiskey replacing the gin and fresh lemon juice in place of lime.

The Last Word is a gin-based prohibition-era cocktail which was rediscovered in 2004 and becoming a cult hit in the Seattle area.
ba-final-ward.garnish: Cocktail cherry at the bottom of the glass

ba-fiore-di-francia.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients in a mixing glass, add ice and stir.
2. Strain into a coupe.
3. Express the lemon peel and discard.
ba-fiore-di-francia.description: In this cocktail recipe Italian amaro, Cynar, joins forces with St-Germain in a nod to the border zone where elderflower grows freely.

ba-first-frost.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously until well chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish.
ba-first-frost.description: Even though carrots are available year round, Isai Xolapa, beverage director of W Philadelphia's Living Room, wanted to celebrate how the veggie can lend an earthy warmth and a natural sweetness to cocktails. He layers the flavors with the slow heat of a homemade honey syrup infused with cloves and jalapeños.

ba-five-point-palm-exploding-heart-techn.method_text:
1. In a mixing glass, combine the ingredients
2. Stir until chilled
3. Strain over ice into a rocks glass
ba-five-point-palm-exploding-heart-techn.description:
This smoky, bittersweet cocktail combines mezcal’s earthy intensity with the bitter depth of Punt e Mes and the richness of coffee liqueur. Chocolate bitters tie everything together with a roasty, slightly bitter finish. A brooding, complex drink with martial-arts-level impact—sip slowly and with respect.

Created by Erick Castro

ba-flannel-shirt.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel.
ba-flannel-shirt.description: Bartender Jeffrey Morgenthaler of the Clyde Common in Portland, Oregon, created the Flannel Shirt for an autumnal event. Using classic fall flavors—apple, earth, spice and smoke—he whipped up this fleecy, bone-warming drink with the bold backbone of Scotch and a supporting cast of apple cider, St. Elizabeth Allspice Dram and super-bold Averna. Morgenthaler says, “It reminds me of a hot drink that you’d have on Thanksgiving morning—only served cold.”

ba-floppydisk.description: The tricky thing when it comes to low ABV drinks is that the end result doesn’t always give that same feeling of a proper mixed drink. They can easily lack complexity and fall flat. On imbibes website they state this drink is “half the booze and double the flavor” which describes this drink perfectly.

ba-floradora.method_text:
1. Short shake all ingredients except soda water
2. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice
3. Top with soda water and stir.
ba-floradora.description: A little spice and a burst of berry flavor - this highball is perfect for a sunny afternoon.

ba-for-mezcalicus-sake.method_text:
1. Stir all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into chilled glass.
ba-for-mezcalicus-sake.garnish: Express lime zest twist over cocktail and use as garnish.

ba-four-points.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe
ba-four-points.description: A very tropical Last Word. Bright, funky and perfectly balanced.

ba-french-gimlet.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass
ba-french-gimlet.description: A simple 3-ingredient riff on a classic Gimlet. St-Germain Elderflower Liqueur is used as the sweetener to balance the tart lime juice. The French Gimlet highlights the bright, citrusy and floral notes of St Germain.

ba-french-pearl.method_text:
1. In a shaker tin, add the lime juice, simple syrup and mint then muddle.
2. Add the gin, pastis and ice and shake until chilled.
3. Fine strain into a coupe.
ba-french-pearl.description: This cocktail recipe puts gin and pastis in the same shaken drink—along with lime juice, simple syrup and mint leaves.

ba-french-pearl-2.method_text:
1. Combine the lime juice, cane syrup, and mint sprig in a cocktail shaker.
2. Muddle the ingredients.
3. Next, add the Pernod and gin.
4. Fill the shaker to the top with ice and shake well.
5. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-french-pearl-2.description: This refreshing, elegant libation is a tribute to the Beaux-Arts Neoclassical architectural movement of the late 1800s in France, an era in which sipping pastis was quite fashionable. The “pearl” refers to the visual opacity of the drink, an effect referred to as “louching,” which naturally occurs when any anise-flavored liqueur or spirit meets water.

ba-frozen-margarita.method_text:
1. Prepare the glass, if using the lime-salt rim. Moisten half the rim of a double rocks glass with a lime wheel, then dip gently in kosher salt.
2. Combine all ingredients in a blender.
3. Fill a 13-ounce double rocks glass with a heaping scoop of pebble ice (see Editor’s Note).
4. Add ice to the blender and blend until smooth.
5. Pour into a double rocks glass.
ba-frozen-margarita.description: A frozen Margarita cocktail recipe made with tequila, Cointreau, fresh lime and orange juices and raw agave.
ba-frozen-margarita.garnish: lime and kosher salt rim, optional

ba-frozen-mudslide.method_text:
1. In a blender jug, combine all the ingredients
2. Blend until smooth
3. Served in a tall glass
ba-frozen-mudslide.description: Death and Co. bartender, Devon Tarby, reworked the 1980s mudslide. Incorporating ice cream into the mudslide removes the need for ice resulting in a richer flavour.

ba-fumata-bianca.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the grapefruit twist in a collins glass.
2. Add ice and top with club soda.
3. Express a grapefruit twist over the drink and drop into the glass.
ba-fumata-bianca.description: This cocktail recipe is a soft, yet edgy mixture of sweet blanca vermouth, herbal Suze, and smoky mezcal that goes down easy.

ba-garibaldi-spritz.method_text:
1. To an ice-filled Collins glass, add the Campari and orange juice and stir to combine.
2. Top with prosecco and garnish.
ba-garibaldi-spritz.description: This version of the classic Garibaldi cocktail recipe dials back the Campari and tops all with prosecco, turning the classic into a spritz.

ba-gaz-regans-negroni.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.
ba-gaz-regans-negroni.description: In Gaz Regan's nontraditional take on the classic Negroni cocktail recipe, Jägermeister stands in for Campari.

ba-gemist.method_text:
Combine cold ingredients in a glass.
Ingredient amounts are usually eyeballed depending on the glass.
ba-gemist.description: Coming from a german word "gemischt", meaning mixed. Popular in Balkan countries, especially with homemade dry white wines.

ba-gentlemans-exchange.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients except the grapefruit peel in a mixing glass and stir for about ten seconds
2. Pour into a rocks glass over a large cube and garnish with the grapefruit peel
ba-gentlemans-exchange.description: A strong rocks cocktail with an emphasis on coffee and bourbon

ba-getaway-car.method_text:
1. Fill a shaker tin half-full with pebble ice.
2. Add all ingredients and shake.
3. Fill a Zombie mug half-full with pebble ice.
4. Strain into the mug, and garnish with a lime wheel and a sprinkle of ancho powder.
ba-getaway-car.description: Meaghan Dorman's take on the Jungle Bird cocktail recipe swaps in Ancho Reyes for Campari—alongside a kick of ancho chili powder.
ba-getaway-car.garnish: lime wheel and a sprinkle of ancho powder

ba-ghost-coast.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice and garnish
ba-ghost-coast.description: An unforgettable tour of western America in cocktail form
ba-ghost-coast.garnish: eucalyptus leaf and/or banana chip for garnish

ba-gibson.method_text:
1. Stir the ingredients with ice to chill, then strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
2. Garnish with the pickled pearl onion.
ba-gibson.description: More fun than answering who first plopped a pickled pearl onion—instead of an olive, or a lemon twist—into a dry gin Martini is recalling who didn’t. “The Gibson’s history is as mysterious as the Manhattan’s,” says Leo Robitschek, bar director at The NoMad Bar and Eleven Madison Park in New York City. The drink’s origins have yet to be cracked, although the urban sophistication of a Martini paired with a pickled twist has left largely anyone with the last name Gibson receiving credit for the drink. In the early 20th century, graphic artist Charles Dana Gibson is said to have requested a fresh take on the Martini while visiting New York private social club The Players, resulting in the garnish swap. There’s also an allegedly teetotaling Mr. Gibson who dropped an onion into his water-filled Martini glass to differentiate his drink while maintaining appearances among colleagues. Most perplexing of all, the earliest renditions of the Gibson, such as in William Boothby’s 1908 The World’s Drinks and How to Mix Them, make no mention of an onion. Robitschek’s favorite story remains that of San Francisco businessman Walter Gibson, who supposedly slipped an onion into his drink, believing it prevented colds. “I love any story that showcases the health benefits of drinks, although this one may not be true,” he says. Robitschek keeps his Gibsons golden. “The Gibson is one of my favorite cocktails, a Martini variation that, when made classically, adds a vegetal, briny umami flavor to the mix,” he says. As for the unsolved onion, some veggie tales are best left to the imagination.

ba-gin-blossom.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice, and stir to chill.
3. Strain into a coupe glass and garnish with an expressed orange peel.
ba-gin-blossom.description: The Gin Blossom is Julie Reiner's (of Brooklyn's Clover Club) modern play on the classic Martini cocktail recipe.

ba-gin-daisy-new-school.method_text:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, grenadine and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a Collins glass.
4. Garnish with a slice of orange.
ba-gin-daisy-new-school.description: This cocktail recipe is a variation on the basic Daisy formula: a sour kicked up with the addition of seltzer or soda water.

ba-gin-gin-mule.method_text:
1. Combine the lime juice, syrup and mint in a mixing glass and muddle.
2. Add the gin and ginger beer and ice and shake well.
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with mint leaves
ba-gin-gin-mule.description: This cocktail recipe is essentially a Mojito (a rum drink) crossed with a Moscow Mule (a vodka drink), but made with gin.

ba-gin-it.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain into a glass on the rocks.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.
ba-gin-it.description: The Gin & It is a classic cocktail recipe made with London dry gin, sweet vermouth, Angostura bitters. Here's how to make it.

ba-gin-pahit.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Nick & Nora glass, then garnish with the lemon twist on the rim of the glass.
ba-gin-pahit.description: An easy cocktail recipe from Malaysia. The classic drink combines gin, bitters and absinthe, but this simply version forgoes the latter.

ba-gin-rickey.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a highball glass over ice.
3. Top with club soda.
4. Garnish with straw, lemon and lime ribbons and fresh basil.
ba-gin-rickey.description: Andra "AJ" Johnson created this juicy, aromatic Gin Rickey cocktail recipe while consulting for a Mediterranean restaurant.
ba-gin-rickey.garnish: straw, lemon and lime ribbons, fresh basil

ba-gin-tonic.method_text:
1. Add lots of ice to a large cocktail or wine glass and stir to chill the glass. Drain any melted water.
2. Pour in the gin. Add the garnishes. Pour the tonic water onto a bar spoon into the glass (to increase the bubbles). Stir once and serve.
ba-gin-tonic.description: Called a “G and T” or gin tonic in some countries, this refreshing drink is made in countries all around the world. The Gin and Tonic was invented in the 1850’s by British soldiers, who mixed gin with their tonic water as a way to drink quinine (which was thought to cure malaria). Tonic water of today no longer has quinine, but the drink stuck around!
ba-gin-tonic.garnish: Any of the following to spice your cocktail: Lime, lemon, cucumber, mint, orange peel, juniper berries, blood orange slice, rosemary

ba-giving-basil.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake, then double strain into a chilled glass.
3. Spritz with the vanilla tincture, then garnish.
ba-giving-basil.description: Gabe Fountain, lead bartender of Oklahoma City's The Jones Assembly, took the classic Gimlet, added an herbaceous complexity with Italicus liqueur and basil, then rounded out the flavors and texture with pistachio orgeat for an irresistibly smooth sipper.
ba-giving-basil.garnish: Small basil leaf or dried basil blossom

ba-go-to.method_text:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients except the ginger beer
2. Shake briefly with ice to combine
3. Strain over ice into a highball glass
4. Top with ginger beer
ba-go-to.description: Created by Rob Krueger, Extra Fancy, Brooklyn NY.He mentioned this to a guest one night, to which she responded, "Oh, so it's your go-to?" inspiring the cocktail's name.
ba-go-to.garnish: Garnish with a mint sprig and cucumber wheels

ba-godfather-iv.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.
ba-godfather-iv.description: A riff on the amaretto-sweetened Godfather cocktail recipe, this drink adds on walnut liqueur for extra depth and nutty richness.

ba-going-out-west.method_text:
1. Add rye whiskey, mezcal, amaro, and simple syrup to a mixing glass.
2. Add a good amount of ice and string for 20-30 seconds.
3. Strain into an old fashioned glass with a large cube.
4. Get an orange peel, squeeze it to express oils, and throw the garnish into the glass.
ba-going-out-west.description: This smoky sipper is the perfect Wild West-ish twist on the Old Fashioned, featuring rye whiskey, mezcal for a touch of smoke, and Averna amaro for depth.

ba-gold-rush.method_text:
1. Add the bourbon, honey syrup, and lemon juice into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over one large ice cube.
ba-gold-rush.description: Created at famed New York City bar Milk & Honey in the early 2000s, this drink's combination of bourbon, lemon and honey became worldwide modern classic.

ba-good-christian-pear.method_text:
1. Shake with ice
2. Double-strain into a coupe.
ba-good-christian-pear.description: David Burnette, South on Main, Little Rock, Arkansas
ba-good-christian-pear.garnish: Garnish with a pear slice or lemon wheel.

ba-gram-arita.method_text:
1. Rim half of a glass with salt and set aside.
2. Combine first three ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the prepared glass over ice.
4. Float Grand Marnier on top.
ba-gram-arita.description: A Cadillac Margarita served at the Copper Room in Yucca Valley made with reposado tequila, Grand Marnier and lime juice.

ba-grand-armys-amaretto-sour.method_text:
1. Combine ingredients in a cocktail shaker and dry-shake without ice.
2. Add ice and shake again until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass.
4. Express an orange twist over the drink, then discard.
ba-grand-armys-amaretto-sour.description: This Amaretto Sour cocktail recipe from New York bar Grand Army combines Campari, amaretto, lemon juice and an egg white.

ba-grand-collins.method_text: Place ice cubes in a highball glass and add Grand Marnier®, and then fresh lemon juice. Top up with soda water and stir.
ba-grand-collins.description: A riff on a Tom Collins, the Grand Collins playfully swaps out Old Tom Gin for Grand Marnier, creating an intriguing, layered flavour profile to match its lively effervescence.

ba-grapefruit-reviver.method_text: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice. Shake to chill. Strain into the glass. Garnish.
ba-grapefruit-reviver.description: For this take on the Brown Derby, bartender James Sauer of Louisville's North of Bourbon leans into its grapefruit flavor with Malört. High-proof whiskey and rich demerara syrup help balance the strong, bitter notes, while creating a bourbon cocktail with depth.

ba-grasshopper-blanco.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker.
2. Add ice and hard shake to incorporate the cream and chill.
3. Double strain into the glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-grasshopper-blanco.description: Liz Kelley, lead bartender at Cure in New Orleans, created this twist on the Grasshopper that uses blanco tequila to help cut through the drink's sweetness. "I particularly enjoy the bright minerality and citrus notes of a good blanco tequila as a foil to the richer elements of the classic," says Kelley. "Shaking it with fresh mint brings some added freshness as well."

ba-green-eyes.method_text:
1. Dry-shake all ingredients without ice to combine, then add ice and shake again until chilled and foamy.
2. Double-strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice; garnish.
ba-green-eyes.description: Chartreuse ups the herbacousness of this gin cocktail from bartender Andrew Volk. Read more about Portland Hunt & Alpine in our feature on Portland, Maine.

ba-greta-garbo.method_text: 1. Shake all ingredients with ice for 15 seconds. Strain into a 5 1/2-ounce coupe glass.
ba-greta-garbo.description: A Daiquiri cocktail riff adding a few dashes of absinthe to the classic mix of white rum, lime juice and sugar.

ba-grog.method_text:
1. Shake all ingredients with ice.
2. into ice-filled glass.
ba-grog.description:
For over 300 years, the British Navy issued a daily 'tot' of rum, sometimes with double issues before battle. In 1740, as an attempt to combat drunkenness, Admiral Vernon gave orders that the standard daily issue of half a pint of neat, high-proof rum be replaced with two servings of a quarter of a pint, diluted 4:1 with water. The Admiral was nicknamed 'Old Grogram' due to the waterproof grogram cloak he wore, so the mixture he introduced became known as 'grog'. Lime juice was often added to the grog in an attempt to prevent scurvy, lending British sailors their 'limey' nickname.

The 'tot' tradition, which was started by the British Navy in Jamaica in 1665, was finally broken on 31st July 1970, a day known as Black Tot Day, although by then, the 'tot' had been reduced to a meagre two ounces.

I hate to let the truth ruin a good story, but historians now say that grog emanates from an earlier period than Old Grogram.

ba-guillotine.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled and diluted.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-guillotine.description: The Guillotine is a mezcal cocktail recipe from San Francisco bar Stoa that combines the spirit with Cynar and dry vermouth.

ba-gunshop-fizz.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the Sanbitter in a mixing glass. Muddle and set aside for two minutes.
2. Add ice to mixing glass and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a Collins glass over ice.
4. Top with Sanbitter.
ba-gunshop-fizz.description: The Gunshop Fizz was the signature cocktail of the original Rogue Cocktails, self-published in 2009 by Maks Pazuniak and Kirk Estopinal, two bartenders at Cure in New Orleans. It was the drink that first caught everyone’s attention, and no wonder. The improbable Gunshop Fizz uses a full two ounces of Peychaud’s bitters, which is usually used only in dashes. It’s enough to make the same drink’s use of Sanbitter, a bright-red bitter Italian soda, seem almost dull. The rest of the drink includes lemon juice, simple syrup, strawberries, cucumbers and several twists of orange and grapefruit. It was a through-the-looking glass take on the Pimm’s Cup recipe at Chicago’s Violet Hour, where Estopinal had worked.

ba-halekulani.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass and garnish
ba-halekulani.description: A cross between a classic bourbon sour and a tiki drink
ba-halekulani.garnish: pineapple wedge, citrus wheel, or pineapple fronds, for garnish

ba-happy-bastard.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients, except tonic, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Collins glass over ice.
3. Top with tonic.
ba-happy-bastard.description: A lighter take on the Suffering Bastard cocktail recipe that calls on cucumber tonic water in place of ginger beer.

ba-hard-sell.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a coupe.
3. Express a grapefruit peel over the surface of the drink and discard.
ba-hard-sell.description: The Hard Sell cocktail recipe combines gin, St-Germain elderflower liqueur, Malört (Chicago's famous shot) and lemon juice.

ba-harvard.method_text:
1. Combine cognac, vermouth, and bitters over ice and stir until chilled
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass
3. Top with soda water and garnish
ba-harvard.description: A brandy twist on a Manhattan that stands out with seltzer

ingredients.name: Espresso
ingredients.note: freshly brewed, or sub a coffee concentrate

ba-haymaker.method_text: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker, fill with ice, and shake well. Double strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice. Garnish with a large dollop of fresh whipped cream, a sprinkle of Maldon salt, and instant espresso powder.
ba-haymaker.description: This rich combo of rye whiskey, espresso, and cream drinks like a boozy iced latte.
ba-haymaker.garnish: Whipped cream, sea salt, instant coffee powder

ba-heart-of-stone.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to mixing glass with ice and stir.
2. Strain over a large ice cube in a glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-heart-of-stone.description: Stuart Weaver, general manager and partner of Denver's Lady Jane, says this Boulevardier variation was the result of a last-minute menu change at the bar, quickly coming together 30 minutes before service began. "I find it so funny that a cocktail I put five minutes of work into turns out to be one of my favorites and a staple here at Lady Jane," he says.

ba-highland-diver.method_text: 1. Shake all of the ingredients with ice, strain into a mug filled with crushed ice, then garnish.
ba-highland-diver.description: If you thought Scotch whisky would be out of place at a luau, think again. “The Highland Diver brings scotch into a more refreshing, approachable context—something you can enjoy in warmer weather without losing the integrity of the spirit,” says Ryan Liloia, head bartender at Clover Club. The whisky’s smoky backbone plays well with the sweetness and acidity of pineapple and lemon, while the coconut and honey add body and richness to this take on the tropical classic Pearl Diver. “It’s layered, balanced, and proof that whisky can be bright and versatile.”
ba-highland-diver.garnish: Fresh pineapple wedge and grated nutmeg

ba-home-on-the-range.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients into a rocks glass
2. Stir to combine
3. Add a large ice cube and give it all a stir to chill
4. Finish with both a lemon and orange twist, making sure the peel oil is expressed into the surface
ba-home-on-the-range.description:
It’s back to basics with another delicious simple Sasha Petraske recipe!

I have really fallen in love with built-in-glass drinks. These are just constructed and mixed in a standard rocks glass or whatever you’re drinking from, and requires no additional equipment to stir, shake, or strain.

Not only is it ultra simple with fewer things to wash, the extra potency to start sets the mood and anchors your palate for the rest of the drink as you slowly sip. I personally looove the super spirit-forward libations, and this intensity actually helps keep me from drinking it too quickly (often a problem for me for cocktails!). Something about the more rustic nature of it compared to a carefully chilled stirred&strained cocktail just really hits the spot for me.

ba-honeyed-coffee-gin-tonic.method_text:
1. Fill a glass with ice. Stir to chill the glass, then strain out the melted water.
2. Combine the coffee, honey syrup and gin in the glass.
3. Stir to chill, then top with tonic water
4. Add more ice as needed and twist a lemon peel over the top of the drink and use as a garnish.
ba-honeyed-coffee-gin-tonic.description: In the Honeyed Coffee Gin & Tonic from Julia Momose, flavor fireworks happen when cold-brew coffee and the classic gin and tonic collide.

ba-honeymoon.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and shake
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up
ba-honeymoon.description: A bright and balanced sour built on apple brandy

ba-hoodwinked.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake and double strain into a glass over ice.
3. Garnish.
ba-hoodwinked.description: Mixologist Devon Espinosa creates a vacation libation with this pineapple mezcal cocktail for Djinn in Santa Barbara's Hotel Californian. In it, he uses Aperol to play up the bitter notes of the pineapple juice.
ba-hoodwinked.garnish: Harissa spice–coated pineapple slice, 2 pineapple fronds

ba-hot-buttered-rum.method_text:
1. To a tempered mug, add 2 tablespoons of batter.
2. Top with hot water and stir in the spirit to incorporate.
3. Garnish with a cinnamon stick.
ba-hot-buttered-rum.description: At his NOLA bar, Jewel of the South, Chris Hannah relies on a number of flavored batters to kick up the Hot Buttered Rum cocktail recipe.

ba-hot-oaxacan-penicillin.method_text: 1. Add the tequila, mezcal, ginger syrup, and honey syrup to a tempered mug and top with hot water. Garnish.
ba-hot-oaxacan-penicillin.description: Combining ginger, honey, and scotch, Sam Ross's Penicillin cocktail is a natural favorite for winter sipping. But looking to make an even more warming version of the modern classic, Resa Mueller at R&D in Philadelphia switches out the scotch with tequila and mezcal and turns up the heat for this Hot Oaxacan Penicillin. "The temperature brings all of the aromatics of the smoke, agave, and rich honey to your nose," says Mueller.

ba-house-of-gucci-mane.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish.
ba-house-of-gucci-mane.description: When Shane Sullivan of Oz by Oz in Madison, Wisconsin, served a brief stint as a bartender in Ireland he found that the most ordered cocktail wasn't the Espresso Martini but the French Martini. Once he returned to the States, his mission was to create his own take elevating the cocktail's sweet notes. But he rounds them out with an amaro base, sherry, and lime juice.

ba-how-bout-them-salty-apples.method_text:
1. Stir ingredients with ice for 30 seconds
2. Serve over large rock
ba-how-bout-them-salty-apples.description: This drink was made by our friend @anushu802 on Instagram. This is the perfect Fall drink- bitter, sweet, complex, and incorporates apples and Bonal.

ba-hugo-spritz.method_text: Combine everything in wine glass with ice
ba-hugo-spritz.description: As reported by the magazines Mixology and Der Spiegel, the Hugo was conceived in 2005 by Naturns bar manager Roland Gruber (aka A.K.) at San Zeno Bar, as an alternative to Spritz Veneziano, and quickly spread beyond the borders of South Tyrol. Initially, the recipe provided for the use of lemon balm syrup, then in practice replaced by elderflower syrup, more easily available.

ba-humuhumunukunukuapuaa.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with crushed ice
ba-humuhumunukunukuapuaa.description: This Smuggler's Cove original is hard to say but easy to drink. If you're wondering, Hawaii's state fish is the namesake.

ba-hurricane-2.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients to your cocktail shaker
2. Whip shake with pebble ice to chill and dilute
3. Pour over pebble ice into a hurricane glass
4. Top with more pebble ice
ba-hurricane-2.description: The Hurricane was created in New Orleans back in the 1940s. It was created out of necessity, when whiskey was in short supply due to the war. Rum was in abundance, and some suppliers would only sell a case of whiskey if it was accompanied by two cases of rum. Bars then had plenty of rum on hand, which forced them to get creative to move the stock!This drink is large and boozy but you can always halve the measurements for a more responsible version.
ba-hurricane-2.garnish: Garnish with a lemon wheel, or pineapple & maraschino

ba-im-on-fire.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with ancho chili powder and a pineapple leaf.
ba-im-on-fire.description: This take on the spicy Margarita cocktail recipe calls on mezcal in place of tequila and Cholula to up the heat.

ba-income-tax.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker and shake for about ten seconds
2. Strain into a cocktail glass and garnish
ba-income-tax.description: An old-timey double dose of vermouth
ba-income-tax.garnish:
dashes angostura bitters

orange wedge for garnish

ba-industry-sour.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients into a shaking tin.
2. Add ice.
3. Shake for 8-10 seconds.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Enjoy!
ba-industry-sour.description: The Industry Sour was created by St. Louis bartender Ted Kilgore in 2011. By his own account, it was created for another industry person and the thought going into it was simply “what would happen if I put all my favorite things into one drink” usually this thought leads nowhere good but on this occasion it created a legendary drink.

ba-insanely-good-gin-tonic.method_text:
1. Add gin, Suze, lime cordial and bitters to a chilled Collins glass.
2. Top with ice and tonic.
3. Garnish with a lime wheel
ba-insanely-good-gin-tonic.description: A Gin & Tonic cocktail recipe adds a measure of Suze, the herbal liqueur, for added bitterness in the effervescent classic.

ba-irish-maid.method_text:
1. Muddle the cucumber slices in a shaker.
2. Add the Irish whiskey, St-Germain, lemon juice and simple syrup into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a chilled rocks glass over fresh ice.
ba-irish-maid.description: The Irish Maid is a Whiskey Sour variation featuring Irish whiskey, lemon juice and fresh cucumber. It makes the case for whiskey as a summer drink.

ba-italicus-spritz.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except soda to a glass filled with ice
2. Stir to combine and top with soda
ba-italicus-spritz.description: A luscious cocktail that's begging for poolside.

ba-j-tonys-kold-brew-americano.method_text:
1. Fill a Collins glass with ice. Add the first four ingredients and stir.
2. Top with seltzer, then garnish with half an orange wheel.
ba-j-tonys-kold-brew-americano.description: This Americano cocktail recipe combines the Italian cocktail and the espresso drink for a bitter, low-proof serve.

ba-jack-rose.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients with ice and shake
2. Strain into a coupe, serve up
ba-jack-rose.description: This simple sweet-tart classic delivers full on apple flavor

ba-jagerita.method_text: Shake ingredients over cracked ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-jagerita.description: I know it’s a frat boy drink, but unless you’ve had it coming out of your nose at 4 in the morning and can’t physically drink the stuff, there’s no way you can look me in the eye and tell me that you don’t like Jägermeister because you’re a liar and I won’t believe you. Shoot it, sip it, I’ll take it any way I can get it. I even had my eyes opened one late night at Simon Difford’s house (hi, Simon!) when David Cordoba mixed up one of his famous Jägeritas and I practically begged him for the recipe.

ba-jamaican-milk-punch.method_text: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in a sealable container, mix well, then chill for at least 6 hours. Before serving, mix briefly in a blender without ice until light and fluffy. Serve over ice cubes and garnish with freshly grated nutmeg.
ba-jamaican-milk-punch.description: For sweet, creamy decadence, blend up a batch of Jamaican Milk Punch with this easy adaptation from Martin Cate, owner of San Francisco’s Smuggler’s Cove. “It’s yet another wonderful way to enjoy rum—the perfect spirit for before dinner, after dinner ... and breakfast,” says Cate.

ba-japanese-cocktail.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir
2. Strain into a coupe, serve up
ba-japanese-cocktail.description: The Japanese cocktail is notorious for a handful of things: it's a very old cocktail, published in Jerry Thomas’s landmark 1862 book How to Mix Drinks; it was the first mixed drink to be named something other than “Whiskey Cocktail”, “Brandy Cocktail”, or some other similarly obvious epithet; it might be the only cocktail Thomas invented himself; and finally, it was the first cocktail to feature more than a dash of a fancy sweetener, orgeat.

ba-jasmine.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the lemon twist in a cocktail shaker three-quarters filled with ice.
2. Shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with the lemon twist.
ba-jasmine.description: This cocktail recipe by Paul Harrington, was named after his best friend Matt Jasmin. It features gin, Campari, Cointreau and lemon juice.

ba-jimmy-dean.method_text: Fill a shaker with ice. Bruise 3 mint leaves between your fingers, then add them to the shaker. Add bourbon, Bärenjäger and orange juice. Shake and strain into a chilled, ice-filled Collins glass. Top with brewed tea, then garnish.
ba-jimmy-dean.description: This brunch cocktail plays off the classic southern flavors of sweet tea and mint, and adds orange juice, bourbon and honey liqueur to the mix.

ba-john-debarys-singapore-sling.method_text:
1. In a shaker, combine the drink ingredients. Add ice and shake for 15 seconds.
2. Strain into an ice-filled Collins or water glass. Garnish with the pineapple wedge and a cherry speared on a pick. Serve with a straw.


 ## Editors note:

### Grenadine:

Combine equal parts pomegranate juice with granulated sugar in a saucepan, over low heat. Whisk until dissolved. Place in airtight container and keep in refrigerator for up to one week.
ba-john-debarys-singapore-sling.description: Made properly, says deBary, the Singapore Sling cocktail recipe should make a drink that's “juicy, fruity and refreshing.”

ba-juliet-romeo.method_text:
1. Combine cucumber and salt in a mixing tin and muddle.
2. Add all remaining ingredients and shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with mint leaf, 1 dash of rosewater on the mint leaf and 3 dashes of Angostura bitters.
ba-juliet-romeo.description: A gin cocktail recipe that would appeal to gin haters. A mix of gin, lime juice, cucumber, sugar, mint, salt and rose water.
ba-juliet-romeo.garnish: mint leaf, 1 dash of rosewater, 3 dashes of Angostura bitters.

ba-jungle-cruise.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients, except the sparkling wine, to a shaker.
2. Break up 2 ice cubes with a rolling pin or muddler until they are in small pieces.
3. Add ice to the shaker, close, and whip shake until you can no longer hear the clacking ice inside the shaker.
4. Open the shaker and pour in the sparkling wine.
5. Then pour directly into the glass.
6. Garnish.
ba-jungle-cruise.description: This tropical highball with pineapple, gin, Campari, and bubbly is the delicious result of when the French 75 meets the Jungle Bird. "In a way, the Jungle Cruise also embodies the Negroni's legacy, evolving from classic bitterness into a refreshing, modern delight," says Alec Kass, beverage director at New York City's Rosevale Kitchen & Cocktail Room. "Adult jungle juice done right."

ba-jungle-spritz.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except soda to a glass filled with ice
2. Stir to combine and top with soda
ba-jungle-spritz.description: A refreshing apertivo inspired by the classic tiki drink, the Jungle Bird.

ba-ken-burns-effect.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass and stir.
2. Strain and pour into a coupe glass.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.
ba-ken-burns-effect.description: This cocktail recipe is a riff on the Manhattan that swaps vermouth for Dry Sack sherry, a blend of Oloroso and PX and maraschino liqueur.

ba-kentucky-flyer.method_text:
1. Add the rye whiskey, maraschino liqueur and lemon juice to a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass or coupe.
ba-kentucky-flyer.description: Created by San Francisco bartender Sierra Zimei, the Kentucky Flyer is a variation on the classic Aviation cocktail that subs rye whiskey for gin.
ba-kentucky-flyer.garnish: Garnish with 2 brandied cherries and a mint sprig speared on a pick.

ba-keoke-coffee.method_text:
1. In a preheated Irish Coffee glass, add crème de cacao, brandy and brown sugar syrup.
2. Top up with hot coffee, leaving room for cream.
3. Finish with a generous float of whipped cream.
ba-keoke-coffee.description: An updated take on the Keoke Coffee cocktail recipe, which adds brandy to the mix and gets served in an Irish Coffee glass.

ba-keystone-highball.method_text:
1. Fill a highball or Collins glass two-thirds full with ice.
2. Stir to chill the glass, then drain off any water.
3. Pour the tea, St-Germain and whiskey into the glass and stir gently to combine.
4. Pour soda water down the side of the glass so as to retain carbonation.
5. Add ice and top with a final splash of soda water.
6. Express the lemon peel, then discard.
7. Garnish with fresh bay leaf.
ba-keystone-highball.description: Like any thoughtful pairing, this dinner cocktail recipe by Julia Momose can be adjusted to suit the meal at hand.
ba-keystone-highball.garnish: lemon peel, fresh bay leaf (or another fresh herb to complement the meal)

ba-kingston-club.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients, except the soda water, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a Collins glass over ice.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Garnish with orange twist.
ba-kingston-club.description: Drambuie gets top billing in this tropical recipe from Jeffrey Morgenthaler, alongside pineapple, lime, Fernet Branca, Angostura and soda.

ba-kingstone-negroni.method_text: Combine all ingredients and stir with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube and garnish with a long, trimmed orange peel.
ba-kingstone-negroni.description: First created in 2009 by Joaquín Simó, partner at New York’s Pouring Ribbons, the Kingston Negroni was an immediate hit. Simó credits the creation to his first taste of Smith & Cross overproof Jamaican rum. “It’s certainly not the most imaginative thing I’ve ever done—I simply Mr. Potato-Headed rum for gin in a classic Negroni spec—but it still strikes me as strange that the first thought I had when smelling and tasting a huge, funky, estery, hogo-reeking, grilled banana bread, smoking allspice branches–laden brute of an overproof Jamaican rum was wondering how it would work in a stirred aperitivo,” says Simó. “Smith & Cross is no shrinking violet, so it stands up to the bombastic chocolate and bitter orange notes in the vermouth while drying out the Campari’s richness and tempering its bitterness. Further evidence that less can sometimes be quite a bit more.”

ba-kiwi-swizzle.method_text:
Muddle kiwi and syrup in the bottom of highball glass
Add remaining ingredients and crushed ice until glass is about two-thirds full
Stir 20 seconds and top with more crushed ice and garnish
ba-kiwi-swizzle.description: Kiwi is underrated and underused! Tiki is the obvious first cocktail style to work kiwi in to, plus tiki and kiwi are surprisingly similar words... Fun! Chartreuse's herbal explosion is tempered by the unrefined cane character of our Demerara Gum Syrup. This is a stellar and novel tropical cocktail.

ba-kiwito.method_text: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker and gently muddle the kiwi. Add ice and shake vigorously for 10 seconds. Fine strain into a glass filled with fresh ice. Garnish.
ba-kiwito.description: This extra-fruity riff on the classic Mojito recipe swaps out the traditional white rum for a split base of Brazilian cachaça and rhum agricole.

ba-koffie-van-brunt.method_text:
1. Fill a 12-ounce heat-proof mug halfway with boiling water.
2. Drop a small mixing tin directly into the water to create a double boiler effect.
3. Add the rum, Cherry Heering and simple syrup into the tin and let sit while preparing a shot of espresso.
4. Once the espresso is ready, pour the hot water out of the mug and pour the contents of the tin directly into the mug.
5. Add five ounces of hot water and top with the espresso shot.
6. Shake two ounces of cream in a cocktail shaker until thick but pourable and carefully pour on top of the drink.
7. Garnish with grated orange zest and cinnamon.
ba-koffie-van-brunt.description: This hot, rum-based cocktail recipe reads like an unorthodox twist on an Irish Coffee. The drink is topped with a cream float.

ba-la-concha.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in shaker with ice, then shake to chill.
2. Strain over crushed ice in a Collins glass.
ba-la-concha.description: What we wanted most [from this cocktail] was a classic Piña Colada flavor profile, but modeled after the fino sherries we couldn’t stop drinking," says Kalimotxo lead bartender Kate Houser. "Swapping in coconut water for coconut cream and adding in Lustau fino sherry made it light, dry, and completely crushable on a patio. The added perk is that you can have more than one in this Texas heat!

ba-la-dominicana.method_text:
1. Whip together a wet cream using a whisk or stand mixer
2. Add rum and coffee liqueur to a mixing glass and stir over ice
3. Strain into a cocktail glass and float whipped cream on top
ba-la-dominicana.description: A rich, complex, rum soaked upgrade on the White Russian

ba-la-louisiane.method_text: Add all ingredients to a cocktail mixing glass (or any other type of glass). Fill the mixing glass with 1 handful ice and stir continuously for 30 seconds until very cold.
ba-la-louisiane.description: The La Louisiane cocktail is an improvement on the Sazerac! Absinthe, rye whiskey and vermouth make this spirit-forward cocktail a stunner.

ba-la-rosita.method_text:
1. Stir ingredients in a mixing tin with ice
2. Strain into a glass filled with cracked ice and garnish
ba-la-rosita.description: This slightly bitter combination shows how complex a cocktail can be, even when made with fairly basic ingredients.

ingredients.name: Jamaican Rum
ingredients.note: such as Doctor Bird Jamaican rum

ba-lantern-fly.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with candied ginger.
ba-lantern-fly.description: The Lantern Fly is an easy rum cocktail recipe combining Jamaican pot still rum, amaro and lemon and ginger juices.

ba-lavender-espresso.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake.
2. Strain into the glass over a large ice rock.
3. Garnish.
ba-lavender-espresso.description: For her sophisticated and moody variation on the Espresso Martini, LP O'Brien—drink consultant and the winner of Netflix's Drink Masters—introduces a lavender syrup and balances the additional sweetness with Averna. The liqueur's bold flavors prevent "the drink from being just another sweet Martini," she says.

ba-layover-in-paris.method_text: 1. Combine all of the ingredients in an ice-filled wine glass and stir gently to combine, then garnish.
ba-layover-in-paris.description: A simple spritz recipe from San Diego's Alicia Perry suggests a leisurely afternoon in the French capital.

ba-left-hand.method_text:
1. In a mixing glass, combine the ingredients
2. Stir with ice for 15-30 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled stemmed cocktail glass
ba-left-hand.description: Sam Ross created a Manhattan/Negroni mash up known as the Left Hand (bourbon whiskey, Campari, sweet vermouth & chocolate bitters) in the early 2000s. Ross wasn't familiar with the Boulevardier (bourbon whiskey, Campari & sweet vermouth) at the time he created it - almost identical ingredients list but the ratios slightly skewed. Sam favoured the 2:1 Manhattan specs in relation to the whiskey and vermouth. It went on to become a modern classic and was part of a series of "hand" cocktails that the Milk & Honey team created - The Right Hand featured an aged rum, Tres Hand was made with mezcal and tequila, and the Smoking Hand contained an Islay and Highland whisky.

ingredients.name: Agave Syrup
ingredients.note: combine equal parts agave nectar and hot water

ba-lena.method_text:
1. Rim a rocks glass with Tajín and set aside.
2. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the prepared glass over ice.
4. Garnish with a pineapple half-wheel.
ba-lena.description: This cocktail recipe from one of the Best New Bartenders of 2025 merges a spicy Margarita and a Jungle Bird into a tropical mezcal drink.
ba-lena.garnish: Tajín (to rim the glass), pineapple half-wheel

ba-limoncello-spritz.method_text: 1. Build all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ba-limoncello-spritz.description: Limoncello Spritz is a refreshing and easy Italian cocktail made with Limoncello liqueur and sparkling water.

ba-lite-treason.method_text:
1. In a mixing glass, combine the vodka, coffee liqueur and amaro.
2. Stir with ice and strain into a rocks glass with one large ice cube, then top with the whipped cream. Garnish.

Mezcal Whipped Cream: Whip ½ cup of heavy cream with ½ oz. of mezcal until thick, then add rich simple syrup [2:1] to taste.
ba-lite-treason.description: In this twist on the White Russian, Kask bar manager Beau Burtnick plays off coffee’s chocolatey, earthy notes with the addition of amaro and a mezcal-infused whipped cream.

ba-little-italy.method_text: Stir all ingredients with ice for about 20 seconds. Strain into a small chilled cocktail glass and garnish with a cherry or a piece of marinated artichoke heart.
ba-little-italy.description:
Audrey Sanders, mixology royalty, created this drink as a homage to the New York City’s Little Italy neighborhood. We first read about it in Imbibe magazine, where they recommended garnish with brandied cherries and letting a little of the cherry liquid dribble into the glass – a modification we heartily endorse.

Not gonna lie – the Little Italy a love-it-or-hate it flavor. If you’re a fan of bitter flavors and you’re looking for an alternative to yet another Negroni, it may just be up your alley. It really is a superb after-dinner drink, where the medicinal overtones can be explained away as part of the history of the digestíf as a post-meal tummy-soother.

Make sure to have very fresh vermouth on hand for this drink; it’s bitter enough without the acrid tang of old vermouth.

ba-lone-ranger.method_text:
1. Add the tequila, lemon juice and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until cold.
2. Add the sparkling wine to the cocktail shaker.
3. Strain over fresh ice into a Collins glass.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.
ba-lone-ranger.description: The Lone Ranger is a French 75 cocktail made with tequila in place of gin or Cognac and brut rosé sparkling wine.

ba-love-murder.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Double strain into a coupe glass
ba-love-murder.description: Two polarising liqueurs come together resulting in a herbaceous, bittersweet concoction. Served at Porchlight in NYC and created by Nick Bennett. Whilst it does have a decent amount of sugar in the drink the strong flavours keep you intrigued.

ba-lucien-gaudin.method_text:
1. Combine ingredients in a mixing glass and fill with ice.
2. Stir well and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-lucien-gaudin.description: Introducing the Lucien Gaudin. Named for an early 20th century French Olympic fencer, the Lucien Gaudin starts off in the manner of a Negroni by combining gin with Campari. With the addition of Cointreau and dry vermouth the result is a pleasantly bitter drink that is simultaneously rich and dry--a challenging flavor to create which is all the more enjoyable because of its rarity.
ba-lucien-gaudin.garnish: A twist of orange peel is not out of place here.

ba-lust-for-life.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with cocoa powder.
ba-lust-for-life.description: This easy mezcal cocktail recipe combines the agave spirit with palo cortado sherry, orgeat, pineapple and lemon juice.

ba-mamie-taylor.method_text:
1. Add Scotch and lime juice to a highball glass and fill the glass with ice.
2. Top with ginger beer.
ba-mamie-taylor.description: Named for singer and actress, Mayme Taylor, this (inexplicably) misspelled cocktail recipe, is a combination of Scotch and ginger beer.

ba-managers-meeting.method_text: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir. Pour over a large cube/sphere in a rocks glass.
ba-managers-meeting.garnish: use a hand torch to blacken an orange peel over the glass. Rub the peel over the rim of the glass and drop into the drink. Serve.

ba-mango-mule.method_text: Muddle cucumber and honey syrup in the bottom of a cocktail shaker. Add the mango puree and lime juice and shake with ice vigorously. Strain into a copper mug. Top with ginger beer and stir.

ba-maracuya-mojito.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except club soda to a cocktail shaker with ice
2. Shake for 15 seconds and strain into glass
3. Top with club soda and garnish with mint
ba-maracuya-mojito.description: This refreshing, rum based cocktail carries summer poolside/porch-side vibes. As a Cuban mojito riff, it has the essential mojito ingredients like mint, rum, and club soda, but adds tropical flavor with the passionfruit syrup. For extra mint flavor, muddle the mint with the syrup in the bottom of your highball glass. Otherwise, shaking hard for 15 seconds with the mint in the shaker is enough.

ba-margarita-soda.method_text:
1. Rim a Collins glass with sea salt.
2. Add the first three ingredients to a shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Pour into the prepared Collins glass, top with club soda and stir.
4. Garnish with a lime wedge.
ba-margarita-soda.description: The Margarita Soda from Hellbender Nighttime Café combines tequila, agave syrup, lime juice and club soda for a refreshing drink.

ba-maria-mole.method_text:
1. In a mixing glass with ice, stir both ingredients to chill and dilute the mixture.
2. Strain into your desired glass. If using a cocktail glass, chill it beforehand; if serving in a lowball glass, add one large ice cube.
3. Finish with an orange twist.
ba-maria-mole.description: The Maria Mole is a cocktail recipe from Brazil that combines Cognac or other brandies and bianco vermouth in a stirred drink.

ba-marigold-mule.method_text: Fill a highball glass with ice,then add first three ingredients before topping the drink with ginger beer.
ba-marigold-mule.description: The Mexican marigold flower, known as cempasuchil, is traditionally used to decorate Día de Muertos altars, and, in the case of the Marigold Mule, it makes its appearance in the form of a garnish alongside, Patrón Silver, St. Germain, fresh lime juice, and ginger beer.

ba-marseilles-rhum.method_text:
1. Fill an ice-filled shaker tin with rhum, liqueurs, and lime juice and shake until well chilled.
2. Double strain through a fine mesh strainer into a Nick & Nora cocktail glass.
ba-marseilles-rhum.description: The Marseilles Rum is a bright, herbaceous cocktail made with equal parts rhum agricole, Bénédictine liqueur, Green Chartreuse, and freshly squeezed lime juice. Learn how to make this original cocktail from Santa Monica's Pasjoli restaurant.

ba-martini.method_text:
1. Pour all ingredients into mixing glass with ice cubes.
2. Stir well.
3. Strain into chilled martini cocktail glass.
ba-martini.description: This classic is a contentious and sensitive topic with serious Martini drinkers. The way one drinks a Martini is simply a matter of personal preference.
ba-martini.garnish: Squeeze oil from lemon peel onto the drink, or garnish with green olives if requested.

ba-mary-celeste.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake to chill and strain over fresh ice in a glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-mary-celeste.description: The nutty sweetness of orgeat rounds out bitter amaro and tart lime juice in this mezcal cocktail from Travis Parsley, lead bartender of The National Bar in Nevada City.

ba-matador.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a cocktail glass.
ba-matador.description: One of two historic Matador cocktail recipe that have inspired a number of modern riffs, this is Café Royal's equal parts concoction.

ba-medicina-latina.method_text:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all ingredients except the mezcal
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Double strain over ice into an old fashioned glass
4. Float the mezcal atop the drink
5. Garnish with skewered candied ginger
ba-medicina-latina.description: The Medicina Latina is an agave version of Sam Ross' Penicillin. The Penicillin pairs a blended Scotch whisky with a smoky Islay whisky whilst the Medicina Latina pairs a blanco tequila with smoky mezcal. A simple yet delicious riff on the original modern classic cocktail. The cocktail is featured in Sasha Petraske's Regarding Cocktails.

ba-merry-spritzmas.method_text: 1. Add the fig preserves and lemon juice to a shaker and stir until the preserves are at least partially dissolved. Add the Aperol, port, Cognac, falernum, and bitters, and shake with ice. Double strain into the glass, then gently stir in the Prosecco and add fresh ice cubes to fill. Garnish with a lemon wedge on the rim stuck with a cocktail parasol.
ba-merry-spritzmas.description: As a longtime cocktail historian, writer, and now owner of Beachbum Berry’s Latitude 29 in New Orleans, Jeff “Beachbum” Berry knows his way around tropical drinks, but creating a wintry spritz with island vibes for the annual Sippin’ Santa’s Surf Shack pop-up was a different challenge altogether. “How do you do a mashup of Christmas vacation and a tropical island vacation by using flavors that remind people of each but still harmonize in a glass?” says Berry. “In this case, fig jam and port wine fill the winter holiday bill, with falernum and cardamom lending a tropical touch. The Christmas-y flavors and the tropical spices complement one another surprisingly well, especially with the festive spritz of sparkling wine to tie it all together.”

ba-metexa.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
ba-metexa.description: The Metexa is a tequila drink made with blanco tequila, Lillet and Swedish punsch. Here, Cocchi Americano swaps in for the Lillet.

ba-mexican-firing-squad.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
ba-mexican-firing-squad.description: A classic first illustrated in Charles H. Baker’s The Gentlemen’s Companion, the Mexican Firing Squad is a tequila cocktail that deserves attention. It’s served at Ward III in New York City, where bartender Kenneth McCoy says he added it to his summer menu because “it’s fun and delicious and a bit more under the radar than a Margarita or a Paloma.”

ba-mexican-razor-blade.method_text:
1. Add ingredients to a shaking tin with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a coupe, if using, or a rocks glass over fresh ice.
3. Float a cucumber slice as garnish and sprinkle piquín chile, cayenne or other powdered chile on top.
ba-mexican-razor-blade.description: The Mexican Razor Blade is anything but basic. Simple but bold, the recipe is a mix of cucumber, lime, syrup and tequila or mezcal.
ba-mexican-razor-blade.garnish: cucumber slice and piquín chile, cayenne or other powdered chile

ba-mezcal-margarita.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe or into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with a lime wedge.
ba-mezcal-margarita.description: Potent, piquant, perfectly balanced, this simple mezcal Margarita recipe comes from Phil Ward's now-shuttered agave bar, Mayahuel.

ba-mezcal-mule.method_text:
1. Add cucumber slices and agave nectar to a mixing glass and muddle.
2. Add all other ingredients, add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a chilled rocks glass.
4. Garnish with a slice of cucumber, a piece of candied ginger and dust gently with chili powder.
ba-mezcal-mule.description: In this take on a mule Jim Meehan, of New York’s PDT, was set on developing a cocktail recipe with traditional Oaxacan flavors.
ba-mezcal-mule.garnish: 1 slice cucumber, candied ginger and chili powder

ba-mezcal-sour.method_text: Shake all of the ingredients with ice until chilled and the drink is foamy, then strain into a chilled glass and garnish with several drops of bitters atop the drink’s foam.
ba-mezcal-sour.description: Chocolate bitters balance lime’s tartness in this silky mezcal cocktail.

ba-mezchine-head.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake and strain into the glass over fresh ice, then garnish.
ba-mezchine-head.description: This mezcal cocktail "tastes smoky, gingery, and tropical with a nice little bite from Cynar," says Local Republic bartender Jeffrey Talbert.

ba-mickey-finn.method_text:
1. Combine the ingredients in a mixing glass over cracked ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
ba-mickey-finn.description: The Mickey Finn is a classic stirred cocktail recipe combining navy-strength dry gin, vermouth, absinthe and crème de menthe.

ba-midnight-marauder-no-2.method_text: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, strain into a chilled glass, then garnish.
ba-midnight-marauder-no-2.description: This rich cocktail combines rye whiskey, coffee liqueur, curaçao, and a touch of mezcal, making for a perfect nightcap. “It’s amazing to end your night with something that has a lot of depth of flavor to it,” says The Starling bar manager Kaley Brodeur.

ba-mis-mas.method_text:
1. Pour fanta into a glass
2. Float red wine on top
ba-mis-mas.description: Popular drink in Croatian coast towns. Pronounced "Mish Mash"

ba-misis-negroni-sour.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker then dry shake without ice to combine.
2. Add ice, and shake vigorously.
3. Strain into a coupe glass.
ba-misis-negroni-sour.description: This Negroni cocktail recipe turns the classic combination of Campari, gin and vermouth into a frothy sour.

ba-mm-mezcal-montenegro.method_text:
1. Start by stirring all your ingredients together with ice in a mixing glass, ensuring they're well combined
2. Aim to stir for about 10-15 seconds; this integrates everything smoothly without diluting the drink too much
3. Carefully pour this mixture through a strainer into a glass filled with ice, ideally a single large ice block, to keep your drink cold longer with less dilution
ba-mm-mezcal-montenegro.description:
The M & M is a sophisticated cocktail that skillfully combines the deep, herbal flavors of Amaro with the smoky complexity of Mezcal. Served in a cocktail glass, this concoction is a testament to the art of blending contrasting spirits to create a harmony of flavors.

Ideal for those who appreciate a drink with depth and character, the M & M offers a unique tasting experience that seamlessly melds the bitter nuances of Amaro with the rich, smoky notes of Mezcal. This cocktail is perfectly suited for sipping slowly on a relaxed evening, allowing the palate to explore the intricate dance between its bold ingredients.

ba-modern-medicine.method_text: Shake everything except the scotch with ice and strain into a ice filled old fashioned glass, then add a float of Ardberg.
ba-modern-medicine.description: Modern Medicine, the drink, by Jordan Hughes, is just perfect. It’s as if scientists concocted a fusion of a Penicillin and a Paper Plane in a petri dish, to cure whatever is bothering you.

ba-molasses-energy-balances.method_text:
1. Add ingredients to a shaking tin.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a highball glass over crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a cherry and lime peel.
ba-molasses-energy-balances.description: A bright and herbaceous cocktail designed to highlight the unique characteristics of a specific rum. The drink balances the herbal notes of Green Chartreuse and citrus with the rum's rich flavors of dried fruit, citrus zest, and buttery baked goods, resulting in a complex, floral, and fruity profile reminiscent of a fruit and cheese danish.

ba-monks-respite.method_text:
1. Combine the ingredients in a blender and add 10 oz. of crushed ice
2. Blend for 10 seconds, then pour into a coconut shell or double Old Fashioned glass
ba-monks-respite.description: Some drink coconut water to stay hydrated—others because it mixes great with booze. Our 2017 Bartender of the Year, Steven Liles from Smuggler's Cove, is among the latter with this original recipe.

ba-monte-cassino.method_text:
1. Add the rye, Benedictine, yellow Chartreuse and lemon juice into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Fine-strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.
ba-monte-cassino.description: Benedictine, Yellow Chartreuse, American rye and lemon juice shine in this bright, herbaceous Last Word variation.

ba-monte-mule-recipe.method_text:
1. Add the ingredients to a rocks glass, then add crushed ice.
2. Stir to chill.
3. Garnish.
ba-monte-mule-recipe.description: The classic Moscow Mule recipe gets an Italian twist via the addition of Amaro Montenegro.

ba-montenegro-spritz.method_text:
1. Fill a wine glass with ice.
2. Add the remaining ingredients.
3. Stir to combine.
ba-montenegro-spritz.description: The Montenegro Spritz is a refreshing twist on the classic Italian spritz, blending bold bitterness with effervescent brightness. This cocktail features Amaro Montenegro, a rich, cherry-and-spice-infused amaro, balanced by crisp Prosecco and a touch of soda water. The deep, complex flavors of the amaro—highlighting notes of orange, coriander, and clove—are softened by the light, fruity bubbles of the wine, creating a sophisticated yet easy-to-make drink. A sprig of sage adds an earthy aroma, elevating the experience beyond a simple spritz. Perfect for summer sipping, it’s a deeper, more nuanced alternative to the traditional Aperol Spritz, offering layers of flavor that unfold with each sip.
ba-montenegro-spritz.garnish: Sprig of sage, half of an orange wheel, dehydrated grapefruit wheel

ba-more-supreme.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients, except Campari, in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
3. Slowly pour Campari against the inside edge of the glass.
