4. Garnish with freshly cracked black pepper.
ba-more-supreme.description: The first cocktail recipe Alec Bales landed on the Ticonderoga Club menu, the More Supreme hews closely to the Daiquiri blueprint.

ba-morning-glory-fizz.method_text: 1. Combine the whiskey, lemon juice, lime juice, sugar syrup, absinthe and egg white in a cocktail shaker and dry shake to combine. Add a scoop of ice and shake very hard for at least 30 second, then strain into an ice-filled glass. Top with 1 or 2 ounces of club soda, to taste.
ba-morning-glory-fizz.description: The Morning Glory Fizz is a classic breakfast cocktail made with whiskey, citrus juice, absinthe, egg white and soda.

ba-mosquito.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with candied ginger.
ba-mosquito.description: The Mosquito is an easy mezcal cocktail recipe from New York bar Attaboy. It combines the agave spirit, Campari and lemon and ginger juice.

ba-mr-brown.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.
ba-mr-brown.description: A modern Manhattan cocktail recipe, a combination of bourbon, Coffee Heering, and vanilla syrup served on the rocks.

ba-mule-in-paradise.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except club soda to a cocktail shaker
2. Short shake for 5 seconds and strain into a rocks glass filled with ice
3. Top with club soda and stir
ba-mule-in-paradise.description: The tart tang of passionfruit helps transports a classic Kentucky Mule build to the tropics.

ba-mulled-wine.method_text:
Put everything except the rum into a pot and heat slowly on low/lowest heat, lid off. The longer this takes, the better, as the spices should infuse into the wine.

Do not boil!

Once hot, stir in the sugar until dissolved.

Add rum.

Strain and serve.
ba-mulled-wine.description: Mulled Wine, or Hypocras, is one of those drinks that predates the era of cocktails. The earliest mentions of heated, spiced wine date back to ancient Rome. Right after they built all those roads, they used them to bring mulled wine all over Europe. It's been a common tradition in Germany, France, and England ever since and is especially popular around Christmas time. ⁣ ⁣

ingredients.name: Orange juice
ingredients.note: Eckroth uses Cara Cara navel oranges

ingredients.name: Espresso
ingredients.note: or 2 oz. strongly brewed coffee, cooled

ba-navel-duties.method_text: 1. Shake the first 3 ingredients without ice, then pour into an ice-filled highball glass. Add sparkling water until almost full, then float espresso on top. Garnish.
ba-navel-duties.description: Bold espresso and bright citrus play well together in this spirit-free riff on the Mai Tai from barista Morgan Eckroth.

ba-navy-grog.method_text:
1. Put all the ingredients in a blender. Flash-blend for 3 to 5 seconds. Pour into a glass. Serve with an ice cone around straw.
2. Ice Cone“This was the signature Navy Grog garnish throughout Tiki’s midcentury golden age. Prep the cone in advance with a Beachbum Berry Navy Grog Ice Cone Kit. (Or you can just pack a pilsner glass with finely shaved ice, run a chopstick through the middle to make a hole for the straw, then remove the cone from the glass and freeze the cone overnight. I won’t take it personally. Well, maybe just a little bit.)”—Jeff “Beachbum” Berry
ba-navy-grog.description: In the March/April 2024 issue, Jeff "Beachbum" Berry shares the cocktail that "upended and uprooted [his life], giving it an unexpected—but entirely welcome—second act": the Navy Grog. While his recipe for his New Orleans bar Latitude 29 is top secret, he shared a "general public" version for home bartenders to shake up.

ba-needle-in-the-hay.method_text:
1. Combine the ingredients into your mixing glass
2.  Stir for 20-30 seconds with ice
3. Strain over fresh ice into an old fashioned glass
ba-needle-in-the-hay.description: The Needle in the Hay was created by Los Angeles-based mixologist Devon Tarby. She was a contributor to the well known cocktail book, Cocktail Codex (from the authors and owners of Death & Co). This Islay whisky cocktail is what you would imagine a Autumn cocktail to be - smoky, sweet maple flavours and undertones of apple from the brandy.
ba-needle-in-the-hay.garnish: Garnish with a twist of lemon

ba-negroni-sbagliato.method_text: 1. Combine vermouth and Campari in an ice-filled glass. Top with sparkling wine, stir to combine and garnish.
ba-negroni-sbagliato.description: The Negroni Sbagliato is said to be the result of a busy bartender mistakenly using sparkling wine instead of gin in a Negroni. Sbagliato means "messed up" or "mistaken" in Italian.

ba-negroni-tredici.method_text: Add ingreds to mixing glass and stir with ice to chill; strain into rocks glass over large cube, garnish.
ba-negroni-tredici.description: Delicious riff. A bit smoother, less bitter, less sweet and more citrusy than the standard version.

ba-negroski.method_text: 1. Stir all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass

ba-neruda.method_text: Shake the first 3 ingredients together, then pour into an ice-filled glass and top with chilled soda water. Garnish.
ba-neruda.description: This spirit-free highball skips the booze but not the flavor. “It’s a liquid play on a Sour Patch candy,” says Lore head bartender Marina Markovic. “It’s sweet, refreshing, and gives just enough kick.”

ba-new-fashioned.method_text:
1. Place a sugar lump in a glass and add the bitters and Cocchi Americano; muddle to dissolve the sugar.
2. Add the sake and fill glass with crushed ice, then stir to combine.
3. Pour the wine over a spoon to “float” atop the drink, creating two layers.
ba-new-fashioned.description: This eye-catching spin on the Old Fashioned combines junmai (pure-rice) sake with Italian aperitivo Cocchi Americano and dry red wine.

ba-nice-by-way-of-antibes.method_text:
1. Fill a cocktail shaker halfway with ice. Add the gin, Benedictine and grapefruit juice. Shake well, then double-strain into a highball glass filled with ice cubes.
2. Top with sparkling water and stir gently. Garnish with the twist of lime peel.
ba-nice-by-way-of-antibes.description: The Antibes cocktail was one of the first of Jason Wilson's favorites, published in this column six years ago.

ba-night-nurse.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass and stir with ice to chill.
2. Strain into a double rocks glass with a large ice cube, then garnish.
ba-night-nurse.description: A layered, tropical Negroni, the Night Nurse builds on a base of Jamaican rum, dials up the bitterness with a splash of Cynar, and adds complementary hints of coffee and banana.

ba-non-alc-hurricane.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients, except club soda, to a shaker
2. Add ice and shake for 10 seconds
3. Pour into hurricane glass and top with club soda
4. Garnish with maraschino cherry or orange wheel
ba-non-alc-hurricane.description: The Hurricane is a classic New Orleans cocktail that features passionfruit and plenty of rum. It was made famous at Pat O’Briens, a popular New Orleans spot that still attracts visitors to this day. In our non-alcoholic hurricane recipe, we’ll be using passionfruit syrup, as well as grenadine to achieve a fruity, tropical flavor.

ba-norwegian-paralysis.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over fresh cracked ice.
ba-norwegian-paralysis.description:
Scandinavian aquavit is not the first spirit that comes to mind when thinking about tropical tiki libations. However, Martin Cate managed to blend this distinct flavoured spirit into a fruity and indulgent cocktail seemingly with ease and the result is remarkable.

Aquavit lays a solid foundation for the cocktail with unmistakable notes of caraway and anise, which are then paired with gentle sweet citrus of orange and vibrant fruitiness of pineapple. Lemon juice introduces a touch of bright and refreshing tartness later balanced by deep molasses of demerara syrup and almond nuttiness of orgeat.

All in all, Norwegian Paralysis is a quite unique tiki cocktail with rather complex flavour profile. Delicious to the very last drop.
ba-norwegian-paralysis.garnish: Garnish with skewered cherry, sprig of mint and an orange twist.

ba-not-far-from-a-tree.method_text:
1. Slap the mint leaves to release the aroma.
2. In a cocktail glass, combine mint leaves with all other ingredients.
3. Add crushed ice until the glass is at least half full.
4. Swizzle until the ingredients are fully mixed and chilled.
5. Top with more crushed ice.
6. Garnish with a sprig of mint and a pear fan.
ba-not-far-from-a-tree.description: A unique swizzle cocktail that reinvents the Chartreuse Swizzle with a Northern French spin, built on a base of calvados and yellow Chartreuse. Pear nectar provides deep fruitiness, mint adds freshness, and lime juice offers a tart kick, all balanced into a refreshing, flavor-packed drink.
ba-not-far-from-a-tree.garnish: Mint sprig and a pear fan

ba-nuclear-daiquiri.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into a coupe or cocktail glass.
ba-nuclear-daiquiri.description: The Nuclear Daiquiri combines green Chartreuse, overproof rum, lime juice and falernum. This cocktail recipe is a cult favorite online.

ba-oak-kin.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Express with orange and lime peels and use as a garnish.
ba-oak-kin.description: Big Bar's Negroni Week special is a hybrid of three Negroni riffs in one excellent aperitivo. Bar manager Eugene Lee combines the staff's two favorite Negroni variations—the Kingston Negroni and the mezcal Negroni—with an additional nod to the Rosita. "I fussed with splitting the base, and rather than go with a simple Negroni spec, I went for a La Rosita style with both sweet and dry vermouth," he says.

ba-oaxaca-old-fashioned.method_text: Combine all the ingredients except the orange twist in an Old Fashioned glass filled with one large ice cube. Stir until chilled. To top with a flamed orange twist, carefully hold a piece of orange peel about the size of a silver dollar, skin side down, over the drink. Light a match and use it to warm the skin side of the peel. Holding the match a few inches above the drink, quickly squeeze the peel in the direction of the match. The oil from the peel will briefly ignite, landing over the drink’s surface.
ba-oaxaca-old-fashioned.description: A Mexican-accented Old Fashioned riff, created by Phil Ward, mixes reposado tequila with mezcal and mole bitters.

ba-oaxacanite.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients in your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice for 12-15 seconds
3. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass
ba-oaxacanite.description: Sasha Petraske wasn't a huge fan of mezcal cocktails as he believed it was too dominate in cocktails. Whilst working at the John Dory Oyster Bar, where Sasha was consulting, Ben Long set forth to change this with the Oaxacanite with great success.A tequila and mezcal split base version of a Bees Knees, almost.Featured in Sasha Petraske Regarding Cocktails.
ba-oaxacanite.garnish: Garnish with a twist of grapefruit

ingredients.name: Gin
ingredients.note: preferably Hayman's London dry or Thomas Dakin Red Cole

ba-obituary.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir to chill.
3. Strain into a chilled Martini glass.
4. Express and discard the lemon twist.
ba-obituary.description: A drier take on the lesser-known New Orleans Martini cocktail recipe from popular Brooklyn bar Maison Premiere.

ba-ol-poets-smoke.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a highball glass.
2. Add ice, and top with soda.
ba-ol-poets-smoke.description: Chumley's cocktail recipe is a mix of Glenlivet Founder’s Reserve, honey, lemon and Amaro Montenegro that drinks like a Penicillin highball.

ba-old-fashioned-romance.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients in a rocks glass
2. Add 1-3 large pieces of ice and stir for 20 seconds
ba-old-fashioned-romance.description: Deep chocolate and rich pomegranate notes flirt with aged brandy in this delicious after dinner drink.

ba-old-friend.method_text:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe glass
ba-old-friend.description: Created by Jim Meehan for the fall menu at Chef’s Club in Aspen, Colorado.The Old Friend is a distant cousin of the whiskey-based Old Pal classic cocktail. Meehan states that Beefeater works perfectly but most London dry gins will work too. Likewise, white, yellow or ruby red grapefruit will all work too but you may need to adjust the balance based on the acidity/sweetness of your grapefruit.

ba-old-haitian.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a swizzle glass over crushed ice.
2. Garnish with a bouquet of mint.
ba-old-haitian.description: Orlando Franklin McCray's update on the modern classic, the Old Cuban, calls on a base of Haitian clairin and gets served over crushed ice.

ba-old-pal.method_text: Combine the whiskey, vermouth, and Campari in a cocktail mixing glass (or any other type of glass). Fill the mixing glass with 1 handful ice and stir continuously for 30 seconds.
ba-old-pal.description: The Old Pal cocktail is a three ingredient cocktail that’s sleek and sippable, balancing bitter and sweet with fiery whiskey.

ba-old-salt.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker, but do not shake.
2. Pour directly over ice into a 10-ounce Collins glass.
ba-old-salt.description: A cross between the Paloma and Salty Dog cocktails, this gin or tequila drink recipe calls for fluffy grapefruit juice and saline solution.
ba-old-salt.garnish: Garnish with an oversized salted grapefruit wedge on top.

ba-padua-paloma.method_text:
1. Combine first four ingredients in a Collins glass over ice.
2. Top with sparkling water, and stir with a straw.
3. Garnish with dehydrated grapefruit wheel and black salt.
ba-padua-paloma.description: This Paloma-meets-spritz mashup cocktail recipe introduces Italian bitter Aperol into the mix. Sparkling water lengthens the drink.
ba-padua-paloma.garnish: dehydrated grapefruit wheel, pinch of black salt

ba-painkiller.method_text:
1. Add the rum, pineapple juice, orange juice, and cream of coconut to a shaker with cubed ice and shake vigorously but briefly to combine.
2. Strain into a hurricane glass or snifter over crushed ice.
3. Garnish with freshly grated nutmeg and a pineapple wedge. Serve with a straw.
ba-painkiller.description: The Painkiller combines dark rum, pineapple juice, cream of coconut, and orange juice to create a refreshing drink perfect for the beach.

ba-painkiller-the-mothership.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients except the tonic water to a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Briefly shake, then pour everything into a double Old Fashioned glass.
3. Add more crushed ice, then top with chilled tonic water.
4. Garnish.
ba-painkiller-the-mothership.description: For this spirit-free Painkiller recipe, Mothership owner Ricky Ramirez introduces tonic water to the mix. “It adds a bittering effect where you’d never know it’s nonalcoholic,” he says.

ba-palmetto-no-1.method_text:
1. Stir with ice.
2. Strain into a coupe.

ba-pancho-villa.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a chilled highball glass over ice.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Garnish with pineapple leaf, lime zest and lime wheels.
ba-pancho-villa.description: This easy-drinking, semi-tropical cocktail recipe by Charles H. Baker is the Philippines’ answer to a Singapore Sling
ba-pancho-villa.garnish: pineapple leaf, lime zest, lime wheels

ba-paper-airplane.method_text: Build all ingredients in cocktail shaker. Shake vigorously with ice. Strain up into coupe or Nick and Nora glass and finish with lime zest.
ba-paper-airplane.description: Mezcal riff on the classic Paper Airplane cocktail

ba-paris-is-burning.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice in a cocktail shaker and shake
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up
ba-paris-is-burning.description: A mixed-based pineapple drink that effortlessly blends island and mainland styles

ba-parisian-dispatch.method_text: 1. Add the first 3 ingredients to a chilled glass with ice. Stir to combine. Add more ice to fill, and top with chilled soda water. Garnish.
ba-parisian-dispatch.description: Blanc vermouth lends an herbaceous base to this elegant mix from Sother Teague. “Make it a Royale by substituting Champagne” for the soda water, Teague suggests.

ba-parisien-mojito.method_text:
1. Muddle mint in glass
2. Add other ingredients
3. Half fill glass with crushed ice and stir with bar spoon
4. Fill glass to brim with more crushed ice
5. Serve with straws

ba-pasion.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except the soda to shaker with ice
2. Shake for 10 seconds
3. Strain into Collins glass over large ice column
4. Top with club soda
ba-pasion.description: Cocktail by @subtletiki. We mess around with highballs all year round, but especially in the summer months. This cocktail is a regular in the rotation. It features mezcal alongside Aperol, passionfruit syrup, and soda water. Super refreshing.

ba-pearl-diver.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a blender, starting with the Gardenia Mix and finishing with the ice.
2. Blend at a high speed for 15 seconds.
3. Strain through a medium-mesh wire sieve into a Pearl Diver glass, pressing gently on the solids to express all the liquid.
4. Add crushed ice ice to fill the glass.
5. Garnish with a geranium leaf.
ba-pearl-diver.description: The legendary Donn Beach’s cocktail recipe is a tiki take on the Hot Buttered Rum, featuring the honey and butter-based Gardenia Mix.

ba-pegu-club.method_text:
1. Gather the ingredients.
2. Pour the ingredients into a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
3. Shake well.
4. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
5. Garnish with a lime wedge or twist. Serve and enjoy.
ba-pegu-club.description: A classic sour, the Pegu Club Cocktail is a fantastic gin drink with orange and lime accents. Get the recipe and mix up this old-school favorite.

ba-petes-word.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-petes-word.description:
Last Word is a famous classic cocktail, that inspired countless riffs and variations. It is often chosen as starting point by many bartenders, proving versatility of this cocktail template. It is particular favourite of Phil Ward, who also created this particular cocktail – Pete’s Word.

Pete’s Word sticks to the original in all aspects, but one – base spirit. Gin has been replaced by Islay scotch, taking the cocktail into a new direction. Whisky brings darker, deeper notes of oak, peat and smoke which pair great with dark chocolate and cherry of maraschino liqueur. Cocktail is further enriched by complex botanicals of the green chartreuse and balanced by a healthy dose of tart lime juice.

All in all, Pete’s Word is a complex delicious cocktail that stays true to its predecessor. Fantastic example of how to apply Mr. Potato Head approach to making new cocktails.
ba-petes-word.garnish: Garnish with a twist of lime and a dehydrated lime wheel.

ba-picante-de-la-casa.method_text:
1. Cut a small piece of chili (about ¼ inch wide) and press with muddler in the shaker tin.
2. Hand clap the cilantro (to release the aroma, place the leaves or sprig in one hand and gently smack it with the other – this warms up the garnish slightly and starts to extract the oils before you use it), and drop in.
3. Add the rest of the ingredients, shake and fine strain into an ice-filled rocks glass (a short tumbler used for serving spirits).
4. Cut off the top end  the chili pepper and place – stem upwards – on top.
ba-picante-de-la-casa.description: Lovers of the margarita, we have a treat for you here! The Picante de la Casa Cocktail, also called the Soho House Picante or Soho House Tonic, is a creation of the Soho House Club. That is a group of private members' clubs with its origin in Soho in the Londoner West End. The cocktail, however, does not have its roots in England but in West Hollywood, USA. -Although, actually, it looks like it could be straight out of Mexico.
ba-picante-de-la-casa.garnish: Top end (stem) of the chilli pepper

ba-pimms-cup.method_text: Build in the order given in a tall ice-filled glass, adding the fruits and cucumber at the end and stirring gently to submerge.
ba-pimms-cup.description: The Pimm's cup is a cocktail that is popular in England, in the United Kingdom. It is one of numerous fruit cups, a type of cocktail with gin, a soft drink, and fruit. Its primary spirit is Pimm's No. 1 Cup, a gin-based beverage flavoured with fruits and spices invented around 1823 as a health drink. The Pimm's cup is the official cocktail of many summer events in England, including the Chelsea Flower Show, the Henley Royal Regatta and the Royal Ascot.
ba-pimms-cup.garnish: Garnish with a french sprig of mint, or a handful of borage or other edible flowers.

ba-pina-verde.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into rocks glass over pebble ice.
3. Garnish with a mint sprig.
ba-pina-verde.description: This Piña Colada riff relies on Green Chartreuse rather than rum. Pineapple juice and lime add a fruity kick, and Coco Lopez adds coconut.

ingredients.name: Saline solution
ingredients.note: 4 parts water to 1 part sea salt

ba-pinch-hitter.method_text:
1. Shake all of the ingredients with ice until chilled and foamy, then strain into a chilled glass and garnish.
2. Ginger SyrupHeat 1 cup of white sugar and 1 cup of water in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and add 2 Tbsp. of grated ginger (with skin). Allow to cool. Add a squeeze of lemon juice and strain out the ginger. If you prefer a spicier ginger syrup, add a few dashes of freshly squeezed ginger juice before straining.
ba-pinch-hitter.description: “This is, truthfully, some version of lemonade,” says Derek Brown, author of Mindful Mixology: A Comprehensive Guide to No- and Low-Alcohol Cocktails. “But I added a few components to make it more complex and compelling.” Together, these components add balance and a spicy spark, as well as depth, complexity, and body, taking a basic lemonade into cocktail territory. Aquafaba is the liquid accompanying canned or cooked chickpeas, and functions as a foaming ingredient.

ba-pineapple-daiquiri.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing tin and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
ba-pineapple-daiquiri.description: This simple and slightly fruity Daiquiri variation incorporates fresh pineapple juice alongside white rum, lime juice and simple syrup.

ba-pink-lady.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Fill with ice and shake for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a chilled coupe
ba-pink-lady.description: A tart, silken drink from the 1930s.

ba-poached-pear.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients except for the spiced wine syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake until the shaker is cold and frosty, about 10-15 seconds.
3. Strain into a large rocks glass with fresh ice.
4. Add the spiced wine syrup by sinking it to the bottom of the glass.
ba-poached-pear.description: It turns out the flavors of a classic French dessert, the red wine poached pear, work beautifully as a fall/winter cocktail. "Cooler weather naturally brings these flavors to the forefront: fuller red wines, baking spices, and pome fruits — evoking the true feeling of the season in each sip," says Siri, lead bartender of Philadelphia's 48 Record Bar. Instead of simply floating his Poached Pear cocktail with red wine a la a New York Sour, he makes a spiced syrup with red wine to imbue it with those baking spices. The result is a cocktail that's dessert-like but not too sweet.

ba-poets-dream.method_text: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass and stir with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish.
ba-poets-dream.description: Manhattan’s Lantern’s Keep adapted this poetic sipper from a 1930s English bar guide. 2 oz. gin 3/4 oz. dry vermouth 1/4 oz. Bénédictine 2 dash orange bitters Tools: mixing glass, barspoon, strainer Glass: coupe Garnish: lemon twist Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass and stir with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish. […]

ba-poolside-gossip.method_text:
1. Add 1 strawberry to a shaker and muddle.
2. Add the remaining ingredients, except the sparkling wine, to the shaker.
3. Shake with ice, strain into an ice-filled glass.
4. Top with sparkling wine.
5. Garnish.

Lemongrass Vodka:
- Add 7 1/2 grams of loose-leaf lemongrass tea to 750ml of vodka or 3 3/4 grams of tea to 375ml of vodka.
- Allow the mixture to steep for 2 hours.
- Afterward, strain out the tea.
ba-poolside-gossip.description: Inspired by summertime memories and photographer Slim Aaron's iconic midcentury "Poolside Gossip" photo, Alicia Perry, beverage director of San Diego hospitality group CH Projects created this sessionable spritz.

ba-poppas-pride.method_text:
1. Add bourbon, ginger juice, lemon wedges and mint to cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a highball or Collins glass over fresh ice.
4. Top with soda water and Angostura bitters (don't be shy about the bitters).
5. Garnish with a mint sprig.
ba-poppas-pride.description: Made with Buck and a Whiskey Smash, this ginger-laced bourbon drink is one of Brooklyn bartender Jay Zimmerman's signature cocktail recipe.

ba-port-light.description:
In the Trader Vic’s tradition, this drink is served in a Port Light glass, which resembles a rounded lantern with red glass and gold trim; the same glass in green is called a Starboard Light glass. A Port Light Highball appears in Trader Vic’s Bartender’s Guide (1947), but it’s very different from this drink, which Jeff “Beachbum” Berry discovered at the Kahiki Restaurant in Columbus, Ohio, in 1996.

Unusual Tiki cocktail. Buffalo Trace works well here. Rye is not recommended for this one.

ba-poseidon.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and stir with ice.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with a lemon peel and olive on a pick.
ba-poseidon.description: The Poseidon served at Crevette in New York is quite different from the sweet blue ’tinis and fizzes floating around the internet with the same name. Strong, stirred and bitter, the riff on the mezcal Negroni mixes the agave spirit with rum, Cynar and Punt e Mes, while saline solution rounds the entire cocktail out.

ba-pousse-cafe.method_text: 1. In a small decorative flute or Pousse Café glass, build the first five ingredients in order. (The ingredients will naturally layer themselves on top of or right under the previous one, depending on density.)
ba-pousse-cafe.description: A pousse-café is now a term for any multi-layered cocktail. The term originally seems to have been a general term for a mixture of liqueurs and/or spirits served after dinner, and most probably originated in France.
ba-pousse-cafe.garnish: Express a lemon twist over the drink and discard.

ba-prado.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake to emulsify the egg whites.
3. Add ice and shake until chilled.
4. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
5. Garnish with a lime wheel, skewered cherry, and a small sprig of mint.
ba-prado.description: The Prado is a sophisticated tequila sour that redefines the classic egg white cocktail. With its base of smooth tequila blanco, vibrant lime juice, and a touch of maraschino liqueur, this drink balances sharp acidity with rich, nutty sweetness. The crowning touch is a velvety foam of egg whites, adding a luxurious texture that makes every sip feel indulgent. Perfect for tequila enthusiasts seeking a refreshing yet complex twist on a timeless classic.
ba-prado.garnish: Lime wheel, skewered cherry, small sprig of mint

ba-prime-inspector.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir for 30-45 seconds.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish with an orange twist and a cherry.
ba-prime-inspector.description: Winter is a high time for strong, boozy stir-down cocktails and Prime Inspector is a perfect candidate for that. Boulevardier inspired blend of apple brandy, amaro and vermouth. Delicious and remarkably enjoyable.

ba-prince-charles-dont-surf.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients except beer, and shake with ice.
2. Strain into an ice-filled glass, top with beer and garnish.
ba-prince-charles-dont-surf.description: A riff on the Army & Navy cocktail, this San Diego sipper adds gin and citrus to an orgeat-rich highball topped with beer. The drink’s unexpected elements find a harmonious balance “that creates a refreshingly daytime, sun-is-out drinking experience,” says San Diego bartender David Kinsey.

ba-puebla-york.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir to chill and strain into the glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-puebla-york.description: Imbibe 75 Person to Watch and Puebla-born bartender Victor Lopez celebrates Mexican flavors through his cocktails at New York City's Mixteca, featuring unique twists on classics. But Lopez's Puebla York, named after a Queens neighborhood that's home to the largest community of Poblanos outside of Mexico, marries his native and adopted homes in this Manhattan-inspired mezcal cocktail.

ba-puritan.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a Martini glass and garnish with a lemon twist.
ba-puritan.description: The Puritan is a Martini that's similar to an Alaska. The easy cocktail combines gin, vermouth, yellow Chartreuse and bitters.

ba-queen-of-the-rodeo.method_text: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker along with ice and shake. Strain into a chilled glass. Garnish.
ba-queen-of-the-rodeo.description: This "gussied-up" Cosmo recipe replaces Cointreau and cranberry juice for a mix of grenadine, maraschino liqueur, and grapefruit juice.
ba-queen-of-the-rodeo.garnish: Lime wheel, a dusting of edible pink glitter (optional)

ba-queens-park-hotel-super-cocktail.method_text: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

ba-queens-park-swizzle.method_text:
1. In a tall glass, gently muddle mint leaves with simple syrup and lime juice
2. Add rum and top with crushed ice
3. Swizzle briefly to mix until glass frosts
4. Add more crushed ice, top with bitters and sprig of mint
ba-queens-park-swizzle.description: An old school island drink with a beautiful presentation

ba-quilty.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a double rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with lemon peel.
ba-quilty.description: In this spirit-forward cocktail recipe, smoky whisky, mezcal, nutty amontillado sherry and bittersweet coffee liqueur are paired together.

ba-rabbit-szn.method_text:
1. Add the first three ingredients to a shaker and whip-shake with a few ice cubes.
2. Strain into a Collins glass.
3. Top with club soda, add ice, then float sweet vermouth on top.
4. Garnish with a sprig of mint.
ba-rabbit-szn.description: Blanco tequila, lime juice, ginger syrup and a float of sweet vermouth make up this bubbly, easy cocktail recipe.

ba-rainy-day-fund.method_text: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a glass, add ice, and stir to chill. Garnish.
ba-rainy-day-fund.description: While working on her own White Negroni riff, Courtney McKamey—Weather Up's beverage director—ran into a road block. None of the white bitter liqueurs or aperitifs she had on hand were doing the trick. But then she reached for Italicus. "The soft floral notes with the citrus bergamot flavors was exactly what I was looking for; it paired beautifully with mezcal," she says. "Italicus saved the cocktail right when I was about to give up."

ingredients.name: Dark Rum
ingredients.note: such as El Dorado 12, Hampden Estate or Goslings Black

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.note: to taste (depending on the sweetness of the falernum

ba-ranglum.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
2. Strain into an ice-filled rocks glass.
3. Garnish with a lime wedge.
ba-ranglum.description: The Ranglum was invented by bartender Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro in Berlin in the aughts and has since become a known entity at craft cocktail bars across Germany. While it remains a relative rarity in the States, it is perhaps only a matter of time before its challenges are embraced by a new generation of bartenders. Despite its complexities of flavor, it is a drink that thrives on the combination of a few simple ingredients. As de Sousa Monteiro summarizes: “You just need them in perfect balance.”

ba-rattlesnake.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and dry shake, without ice.
2. Add ice and shake again until chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a coupe glass.
ba-rattlesnake.description: The Rattlesnake is a classic whiskey cocktail recipe combining rye, absinthe, lemon juice, simple syrup and an egg white.
ba-rattlesnake.garnish: Garnish with an Angostura bitters swirl.

ba-reading-nook.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker and dry shake vigorously for 45 seconds.
2. Add ice and shake again for 15 to 30 seconds to fully chill.
3. Strain into the glass.
4. Express orange oil atop the drink before serving.
5. Garnish.
ba-reading-nook.description: The type of coffee used greatly impacts the flavor of this spirit-free coffee drink from 2025 Imbibe 75er Morgan Eckroth. "I would suggest a fruit-forward coffee, roasted light-medium," Eckroth says. "Something like a natural Ethiopian or Colombian coffee would work well."

ba-real-charmers-daiquiri.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients in a shaker and hard shake with ice.
2. Double-strain into Nick and Nora glass.
ba-real-charmers-daiquiri.description: The nuclear Daiquiri cocktail recipe served at Los Angeles bar Real Charmer combines rum, green Chartreuse, coconut syrup and lime juice.

ba-red-hook.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and stir
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, serve up
ba-red-hook.description: This contemporary Manhattan riff is a balanced people-pleaser

ba-red-morning-light.method_text:
1. Stir all of the ingredients in a mixing glass with ice until chilled.
2. Strain into a glass holding a large ice cube.
3. Use an atomizer to spray the drink with a smoky scotch, then garnish. (Alternately, drip several drops of scotch atop the drink, then garnish.)
ba-red-morning-light.description: Smoky scotch and bittersweet Campari combine for the perfect cold-weather sipper from Vegas.

ba-remember-the-alimony.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients except the orange twist in a rocks glass filled with one large piece of ice.
2. Stir until chilled, about 30 seconds.
3. Express an orange twist over the drink and drop into the glass.
ba-remember-the-alimony.description: A split base of fino sherry and Cynar are finished with a measure of gin for a thoroughly modern sherry cocktail recipe.

ba-reno.method_text:
1. Throw all ingredients with ice.
2. Strain into over a large cube ice.
3. Garnish.
ba-reno.description: The story which inspired this cocktail took place during WWII on 21st April 1945, when the allied forces planned to retake Bologna. Polish, English, American and French troops helped Italian partisans to capture the city in a very unusual battlefield, a river called Reno. I used ingredients that remind me of the forces involved in the battle. Amaro Montenegro symbolises the city. Cocchi Americano to celebrate the partisan's movement born in Asti. Italicus represents braveness. And finally, Suze, this sophisticated liqueur de gentian, used to remember the aid received by the allies. Without this strong bitter touch, my cocktail wouldn't be the same, and the battle wouldn't have been won!

ba-revolver.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients over ice and stir around 15 seconds
2. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish
ba-revolver.description: A San Francisco original, and an exceptional coffee-laced riff on the Manhattan

ba-rib-tickler.method_text:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all ingredients
2. Shake briefly with ice to combine
3. Strain over ice into a wine glass
4. Top with soda water
ba-rib-tickler.description: Created by Alex Day, Nitecap, NYC.This drink was born out of the idea to create a more sippable, bubbly White Negroni (which is Suze, gin, and Lillet Blanc or blanc vermouth).

ba-ric-pear-blanc.method_text:
1. Shake all of the ingredients without ice until foamy, then add ice to the shaker and shake again until chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled glass, and garnish.
ba-ric-pear-blanc.description: Wine-based cocktails are the primary stock-in-trade at Sacramento bar and restaurant Ro Sham Beaux, and this drink accents blanc vermouth’s floral, fruity characteristics with the flavors of pear and ginger.

ba-risorgimento-ditalia.method_text:
1. Combine the first four ingredients in a Collins glass, then stir and add spear ice (or cubes).
2. Using an atomizer, spritz the absinthe over the top of the drink.
3. Garnish with an orange slice sprinkled with salt.
ba-risorgimento-ditalia.description: A more spiritous twist on the Garibaldi cocktail recipe, this drink sees additions of gin and absinthe to the orange juice and Campari.

ba-ritz-cocktail.method_text: 1. Combine the first 4 ingredients in a shaker and fill with ice. Shake well to chill, then strain into a chilled glass. Top with Champagne and garnish.
ba-ritz-cocktail.description: Dale DeGroff raised the cocktail flag over New York during his tenure at the Rainbow Room in the 1980s and '90s. His Ritz Cocktail, created while working at Aurora in 1985, bears the DNA of traditional classics, and it helped usher in a new wave of talented bartenders.

ba-rob-roy-no-3.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel.
ba-rob-roy-no-3.description: Brian Silva's overhaul of a classic scotch whisky cocktail recipe is inspired by the structure of a "perfect" cocktail.

ba-rocinante.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir and strain over a large cube in a glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-rocinante.description: Named after Don Quixote's horse, this mezcal sipper blends "smoky, bitter, floral, and sweet notes that tell a story of exploration and timeless landscapes," says Aaron Sanchez of Denver's Lady Jane cocktail bar.

ba-rocket-power.method_text: Add arugula into your shaking tin, add ice, and shake for 10 seconds. Add remaining ingredients, shake until chilled. Double strain into chilled glass over fresh ice.

ba-roman-holiday.method_text:
1. Fill a cocktail shaker with gin, Amaro, Campari, pineapple juice, lime juice, and cold brew coffee. Add ice to the shaker.
2. Shake well until the mixture is chilled.
3. Fill a glass with crushed ice.
4. Strain the cocktail over the crushed ice.
5. Garnish with pineapple leaves and a cinnamon stick that's been charred on the edge with a lighter or blowtorch. Serve the cocktail immediately.
ba-roman-holiday.description:
Jungle Bird is a quintessential tiki / tropical cocktail. The combination of blackstrap rum and Campari is incredibly effective, delivering that bitter-sweet satisfaction. Roman Holiday – draws inspiration from this delicious creation and reinterprets it in a rather unique and tasty way. (I have encountered a few different specs for this cocktail. I chose to test this one, simply because I happened to find it first, but there might be other, even mores delicious riffs).

Base of this cocktail is split between London dry gin and amaro Averna. Gin brings dry notes of juniper, touch of coriander, while Averna adds bold herbal flavours with hints of aniseed and chocolate. Campari, provides those bitter-sweet notes of Mediterranean oranges, without which it is hard to imagine the cocktail world. Pineapple juice brings that delicious tropical fruity sweetness with a touch of acidity, while tartness of the lime juice, balances out the cocktail. Last addition of cold brew, increases the cocktail complexity and gives it an almost Americano kind of vibe. Not too dominating, just a subtle touch lingering in the background.

All in all, Roman Holiday, is a rather unique and tasty creation. Drawing inspiration from a tiki classic, yet completely reimagining it. This certainly piqued my interest to try the other available specs for this cocktail side by side, to see which taste best.

ba-rome-with-a-view.method_text:
1. Add Campari, dry vermouth, lime juice and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain over ice into a Collins glass.
4. Top with soda water and garnish with an orange wheel.
ba-rome-with-a-view.description: Michael McIlroy's Rome With a View cocktail recipe falls somewhere between an afternoon appropriate Collins and an Americano.

ba-room-key.method_text: Shake on ice and pour into a Collins glass over ice. Top with Mineral Water and then add all the angostura dashes to the top. Serve with a straw.
ba-room-key.description: It’s basically a Skeleton Key with white rum instead of whiskey.

ba-rubino-tequila-spritz.method_text: 1. Combine the first 3 ingredients in a shaker with ice. Shake and strain into a chilled glass with fresh ice. Top with blood orange soda and Prosecco, then garnish.
ba-rubino-tequila-spritz.description: “The intention behind the Rubino Spritz was to bridge the gap between the palates and desires of our Knoxville audience and our authentic northern Italian brand,” explains Madison Walker, bar manager at Brother Wolf. The ruby-hued spritz complements earthy tequila with the floral and citrus notes of Italian bergamot liqueur Italicus, all amplified by the juicy sweetness of blood orange soda. “The drink is truly a marriage of our identities: Knoxville and Italy.”

ba-rum-and-ramazzotti.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a cocktail glass over fresh pebble ice.
4. Garnish with a few lime wheels, skewered cherry and pineapple spears.
ba-rum-and-ramazzotti.description: This cocktail is an interesting take on the classic Jungle Bird, drawing inspiration from this well-known tiki drink with a couple of key substitutions. It uses a dark rum base with pronounced molasses, caramel, coffee, chocolate, and oak notes, paired with Amaro Ramazzotti which replaces Campari. The amaro adds bitter-sweet flavors of liquorice, cola, oranges, and cinnamon. Generous pineapple juice maintains the tropical theme with sweet and tart fruitiness, while fresh lime juice provides a sharp, tart kick. The result is a slightly deeper, bolder, but nonetheless flavourful and intriguing variation.

ba-rum-old-fashioned.method_text: Add all ingredients to a stirring glass, fill with ice, stir and strain.
ba-rum-old-fashioned.description: The oldest recipe for this cocktail appeared in cocktail guides around 1860 and called for it to be made with gin. A couple of decades later it was made with bourbon, apparently by James E. Pepper, bartender and esteemed bourbon aristocrat, at the Pendennis Club in Louisville, Kentucky. You'll love how delicious the Old Fashioned tastes when made with Reserva Exclusiva. It almost seems like the foundation of the Old Fashioned was laid out with this rum in mind. An incredible mix of rich, bitter and citrusy makes our version of rum a choice for all fans of the old fashion.

ba-rusty-ringo.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir for 60 rotations.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
3. Garnish with gold leaf.
ba-rusty-ringo.description: From New York's Bar Goto, a modern interpretation of the Rusty Nail cocktail recipe made with calvados, Scotch and Drambuie liqueur.

ba-sage-gibson.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir to chill. Add the onion and sage to a chilled glass. Pour the cocktail into the glass.
Sage-Infused VodkaAllow fresh sage (roughly 1 leafy sprig per 8 oz) to steep and infuse vodka for 3 days.
ba-sage-gibson.description: Gary Wallach, partner of Lindens NYC, infuses vodka with one of his favorite herbs, sage, for his take on the Gibson cocktail. "I wanted to craft a cocktail that was an ode to the enduring harvest of the colder months," he said.
ba-sage-gibson.garnish: Pickled onion and fresh sage leaf

ba-saisonniere.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a sage leaf and a lemon twist.
ba-saisonniere.description: The winter version of Lafayette's seasonally changing staple cocktail recipe—hence, the name Saisonnière—is an herbal riff on the basic sour.
ba-saisonniere.garnish: sage leaf and a lemon twist

ba-sakura-martini.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a glass and garnish with a salted cherry blossom.
ba-sakura-martini.description: Bar Goto's Martini cocktail recipe combines salted cherry blossom with maraschino and the dry, vinous quality of sake.

ba-salmoncito.method_text:
1. Combine the first three ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
2. Top with tonic water.
3. Garnish with a supremed grapefruit wedge and a grapefruit twist; express oil from the grapefruit peel and then discard it.
ba-salmoncito.description: This bittersweet, citrusy highball made with gin, Campari, grapefruit and tonic is a Mexico City-born modern classic.
ba-salmoncito.garnish: A supremed grapefruit wedge and a discarded grapefruit twist

ba-sang-amer.method_text: 1. Reverse dry shake (shake hard with ice first and then remove the ice and shake hard again) to achieve a frothy layer. Pour into an ice-filled glass. Garnish.
ba-sang-amer.description: For something light to whet the appetite, mix together this tequila aperitif cocktail from Chemin à la Mer in New Orleans.

ba-sangria.method_text:
1. Chop the orange (leaving the peel on) and apple into bite-sized chunks, then add them to the bottom of a pitcher. Sprinkle them with sugar and stir. Let them stand for 20 minutes at room temperature.
2. After 20 minutes, pour in the red wine, brandy, orange liqueur, and lemon rounds. Stir and refrigerate 1 to 4 hours. (Don’t go beyond 4 hours or the fruit texture starts to degrade.)
3. Pour the sangria into ice filled glasses and top with a splash of sparkling water (if desired). Add fruit to each glass, preferably on long skewers for easy snacking.
ba-sangria.description:
A punch, sangria traditionally consists of red wine and chopped fruit, often with other ingredients or spirits.

Sangria is very popular among foreign tourists in Spain even if locals do not consume the beverage that much. It is commonly served in bars, restaurants, and chiringuitos and at festivities throughout Portugal and Spain.
ba-sangria.garnish: Drop fruit chunks into a glass

ba-saturn.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice
ba-saturn.description: Winner of 1967's International Bartender's Association World Cocktail Championship - The Saturn is ready for its comeback!

ba-sauvignon-blanc-punch.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except the club soda into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a highball glass filled with fresh ice.
3. Top with the club soda and stir briefly and gently to combine.
ba-sauvignon-blanc-punch.description: This vibrant white wine meets its perfect match, Aperol, in Alex Day’s epic punch recipe.

ba-savoy-special-1.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice
2. Stir 20 seconds and strain into a chilled martini glass
ba-savoy-special-1.description: For those who find martinis overly dry, this variation incorporates a hint of grenadine to craft a smoother and well-balanced flavor profile.

ingredients.name: Orange bitters
ingredients.note: equal parts Fee Brothers West Indian Orange Bitters and Regans' Orange Bitters No. 6

ba-sawyer.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass.
ba-sawyer.description: The Sawyer, a cocktail recipe from Ssäm Bar, is an icy, bitters-soaked twist on a gimlet doctored with nearly thirty dashes of bitters.

ba-scofflaw.method_text:
1. Add the whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice, grenadine and orange bitters into a shaker with ice and shake until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
ba-scofflaw.description: The creatively named Scofflaw combines whiskey, dry vermouth, lemon juice and grenadine. It was invented in Paris during U.S. Prohibition.

ba-scorched-earth.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass and stir
2. Strain into a lowball or whiskey glass over ice
3. Flame orange peel (optionally) and garnish
ba-scorched-earth.description: A wild and daring twist on the Negroni

ba-scorpion-bowl.method_text:
1. Put everything in a blender.
2. Blend for up to 10 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a Tiki bowl.
ba-scorpion-bowl.description: The Scorpion, like many tiki cocktails, has gone through countless iterations, from a gin and wine-laced libation to this contemporary version of Trader Vic’s 1946 recipe (even he prescribes several riffs in his own books). It’s difficult to know where the original recipe ends and the contemporary begins, especially when so much rum is involved. But it is thought that, while in Hawaii, Vic first tried the punch from which the Scorpion was modeled, which mostly likely contained okolehao, an indigenous spirit distilled from the Polynesian ti plant. Orgeat is a constant ingredient in most interpretations and is key to the balance of dark rum and fruit.

ba-scorpion-reef.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except the Angostura bitters
2. Half fill with crushed / pebble ice
3. Swizzle until glass is frosted
4. Finish with Angostura bitters and five spice
ba-scorpion-reef.description: The Scorpion Reef is a creation of Marshall Davis from the Gallo Pelón Mezcaleria. Marshall drew inspiration from a smoked pineapple flan that he was working on for the dessert list. He noted that “After swizzling, you’ve got a tropical potion with just enough overproof heat to keep you on your toes with the sensation of caramelized pineapple fresh off the grill.”.

ba-scotch-and-coconut.method_text:
1. A day ahead of making the cocktail, freeze the coconut water in a large ice cube mold.
2. When ready to make the drink, combine the ingredients in a shaker with ice and stir until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over the frozen coconut water ice.
ba-scotch-and-coconut.description: A split base of rum and Scotch might sound like the perfect match for cold-weather sipping, but when curaçao and coconut water enter the equation, the combo takes a turn for the tropical.

ba-scotch-sling.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass over ice and stir until chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
3. Garnish with a lemon peel.
ba-scotch-sling.description: The Improved Scotch Sling is a sour cocktail recipe that gets stirred, rather than shaken. Here, whisky meets honey, lemon and maraschino.

ba-sea-legs.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a Hybrid Cocktail Shaker.
2. Add ice and shake hard for 20 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
ba-sea-legs.description: The Sea Legs cocktail encapsulates "a nautical feel without the kitsch", says its creator Alejandro Olivares. Big smoke flavor from the scotch and mezcal is lightened up with fresh lime and almond orgeat... and don't skip the celery bitters on this one.
ba-sea-legs.garnish: Garnish with a salted rim and lime wheel.

ba-second-serve.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except soda water to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
3. Top with soda and garnish with a half orange wheel.
ba-second-serve.description: As a lower-alcohol, softer-hitting cocktail recipe, this combination of Amaro Montenegro and fino sherry is a Spain vs. Italy matchup.

ba-second-serve-2.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients except soda water to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
3. Top with soda and garnish with a half orange wheel.
ba-second-serve-2.description: As a lower-alcohol, softer-hitting cocktail recipe, this combination of Amaro Montenegro and fino sherry is a Spain vs. Italy matchup.

ba-see-you-on-wednesday.method_text:
1. At the bottom of a shaker, muddle the jalapeño, cilantro, and agave nectar.
2. Add the celery juice, lime juice, and salt solution. Add ice and shake until well chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a Tajín-rimmed double rocks glass over large-format ice.
ba-see-you-on-wednesday.description: This zero-proof Spicy Margarita variation from Natasha David combines celery juice, lime juice, jalapeno, cilantro, agave nectar, and salt.

ba-seelbach.method_text:
1. Add the bourbon, Cointreau, Angostura bitters and Peychaud’s bitters into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled flute.
3. Top with cold Champagne or other sparkling wine.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.
ba-seelbach.description: The Seelbach Cocktail may not be a julep, but it doesn't have to be: it's respectable, powerful, and delicious right down to the bottom of the glass.

ba-sentimental-gentleman.method_text:
1. Stir all ingredients.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
ba-sentimental-gentleman.description: Two Sundays ago, Andrea and I ate dinner at Veggie Galaxy and headed over to Brick and Mortar where bartenders Kenny Belanger and Misty Kalkofen were making drinks. For my first cocktail, I asked Kenny for the Sentimental Gentleman which offered up a peaty smoke aroma from the Scotch that later gained walnut notes as it warmed up. The malt from the Scotch filled the sip, and the swallow was an interplay of the herbal Benedictine and the walnut. Rather poetically, the Sentimental Gentleman got a bit more bitter and sharp over time as it acclimated to room temperature.

ba-seven-seas-swizzle.method_text:
1. Build all the ingredients in the appropriate glass and add half the amount of necessary ice. 
2. Swizzle until the glass is cool.
3. Top with ice and garnish.
ba-seven-seas-swizzle.description: In his recipe, Nick Batavia plays with green tea syrup and lime, for a riff on the Queen Park Swizzle with traditional punch ingredients.
ba-seven-seas-swizzle.garnish: Mint bouquet and dusting of nutmeg

ba-sex-work-is-real-work.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a blender.
2. Blend until smooth and serve in your glass of choice.
3. Garnish with edible flower and mint bouquet.
ba-sex-work-is-real-work.description: Christine Wiseman's cocktail recipe is a take on the frozen Pornstar Martini with additions of umami-forward umeboshi and Champagne acid.

ba-shade-thrower.method_text: 1. Stir all of the ingredients with ice, then strain into a glass filled with a large ice cube, and garnish.
ba-shade-thrower.description: For a less bitter and smoother Boulevardier riff, Freddy Schwenk of Geist in Nashville swapped out the Campari with Averna and Aperol.

ba-shannon-tebays-paloma.method_text:
1. Salt the rim of the Collins glass, then add the Topo Chico and set aside.
2. Combine all the remaining ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into the Collins glass, add ice, and garnish with a lime wedge.
ba-shannon-tebays-paloma.description: Coming in on top in our Paloma tasting was this cocktail by Shannon Tebay of Death & Co. New York, using El Tesoro Blanco tequila.

ba-shirley-temple.method_text:
1. Fill a Collins glass with cubed ice.
2. Add the grenadine and lime juice.
3. Top with the ginger ale and gently stir to combine.
ba-shirley-temple.description: The cocktail may have been invented by a bartender at Chasen's, a restaurant in West Hollywood, California, to serve then-child actress Shirley Temple.
ba-shirley-temple.garnish: Garnish with two skewered Luxardo maraschino cherries.

ba-shliva-sour.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to shaker
2. Shake for 15sec
3. Strain into a glass

ba-shoot-the-moon.method_text:
1. In a double Old-Fashioned glass, combine all ingredients with ice.
2. Stir until chilled and diluted.
3. Garnish with dehydrated pear and dust with cinnamon.
ba-shoot-the-moon.description: A cocktail recipe for a riff on the Gin Old-Fashioned made with Fords Gin and pear brandy and designed to minimize water waste.

ba-siesta.method_text: Shake with ice and strain into a chilled coupe
ba-siesta.description:
This spin on the Hemingway Daiquiri was created in 2006 by Katie Stipe (who's at New York's Vandaag now.) Tequila adds warmth to bitter Campari; it's a luxurious cocktail that's a bit like sipping candied grapefruit peel.

"Katie describes this drink as her first "Aha!" moment when she took a favorite classic cocktail, the Hemingway Daiquiri, and used it as a template to create something new." (Source: Jim Meehan's PDT Cocktail Book.)

For those that might need two cocktails today, you can check out the Hemingway Daiquiri mentioned above, in last year's Advent of Cocktails, here: AoC 2021, Dec 12: Hemingway Daiquiri

ba-sin-cyn.method_text:
1. Add all the ingredients into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
ba-sin-cyn.description: The simple Sin Cyn cocktail combines scotch with Cynar and sweet vermouth. It’s part Rob Roy, part Boulevardier and wholly delicious.

ba-single-village-fix.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice
2. Shake and strain into a chilled coupe.
ba-single-village-fix.description: This three-ingredient mezcal cocktail from bartender Thad Vogler has become a modern classic.

ba-skeleton-key.method_text:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice (or clear ice). Pour in the bourbon, St Germain, and lemon juice. Top with the ginger beer.
2. Shake in 6 to 8 dashes Angostura bitters. Serve immediately.
ba-skeleton-key.description: The Skeleton Key cocktail is the ideal blend of bourbon, elderflower, and ginger beer! This fun drink is easy to mix up right in the glass.

ba-smoke-follows-beauty.method_text:
1. In a shaker, muddle the cucumber and cilantro.
2. Add the mezcal, infused triple sec, lime juice, agave syrup, and ice, and shake until well-chilled.
3. Double-strain into a Nick & Nora glass.
4. Garnish with a chilled slice of jicama seasoned with sal de gusano.
ba-smoke-follows-beauty.description: This mezcal cocktail is both spicy and refreshing, thanks to serrano-infused triple sec, cucumbers, and cilantro.

ba-smokeroni.method_text: Stir all ingredients in an ice-filled mixing glass and strain over large ice
ba-smokeroni.description: Created at The House Of Machines in Cape Town, the SmokeRoni is an Agave Negroni riff that really brings the smoke to the glass. Combining Montelobos Mezcal, Tequila, Sweet Vermouth & Campari this is a drink that captures the depth that you’ve been missing

ba-smooth-kiss.method_text:
1. Shake all ingredients except the soda water.
2. Top up with soda water

ba-snake-bit-sprout.method_text:
1. Shake all of the ingredients except the cider with ice and strain into glass filled with 4 large ice cubes.
2. Top with crushed ice, fill with chilled cider.
3. Garnish
ba-snake-bit-sprout.description: The bar team at Julep commonly taps regional and historic ingredients to make the house drinks. In this refreshing chamomile cocktail, the flowers bring a floral depth to the mix. And did you know chamomile was once used as a southern remedy for snake bites? That's inspired the drink's name.

ba-snake-eyes.method_text:
1. Salt the rim of a large rocks glass.
2. Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker, add ice, then shake until chilled.
3. Fine strain into the large rocks glass filled with ice.
ba-snake-eyes.description: Inspired by the Caribbean combo of blended Scotch and coconut, this cocktail recipe swaps in smoky mezcal in lieu of whisky.

ba-sno-cone.method_text:
1. Whip shake with crushed ice and dump into the glass.
2. Top with crushed ice and garnish with a few generous dashes of Peychaud's bitters.
ba-sno-cone.description: The drink is a visual reference to the vibrant, fruity shaved ice and syrup Sno-Cones served on street corners in the summer. As this was for a winter menu, it has a rich and warming flavor profile. The idea was to create a deceptively seasonal drink, one that looked like summer but drank like winter.

ba-society-street.method_text: 1. Add all of the ingredients to a mixing glass, fill with ice, and stir. Strain the glass. Garnish.
ba-society-street.description: As a nod to the many Manhattan variations named after New York neighborhoods, Jeremy Buck created this Charleston-inspired take on the classic. His Society Street features a bourbon base and a hint of peach in tribute to the South with Cognac for the city's French influence.

ba-sour-strawberry-highball.method_text:
1. Add the tequila and strawberry shrub to a chilled highball glass. Briefly stir to mix. Nearly fill with ice. Pour seltzer down the neck of a barspoon to top. Garnish with a lime wedge.
Strawberry Shrub SyrupWash, trim, and quarter 1 lb. of ripe strawberries. Add to a mixing bowl with 2 cups of granulated sugar and toss to coat. Gently mash the fruit with a fork. Cover and let stand at room temperature for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 1 day (but 2 is ideal), periodically shaking the container to redistribute the contents. Mix in 1 1/2 cups of apple cider vinegar, then strain and transfer the mixture into a resealable bottle, squeezing out as much liquid as you can. Refrigerate and use within 2 weeks.
ba-sour-strawberry-highball.description: Can a compelling cocktail be made with just two ingredients? That's the basis for Roger Kamholz's book Pour Together, which features classic two-ingredient drinks like the Dark & Stormy and the Gibson. But he also includes a few recipes that, although still simple, do require some assembly, such as this Sour Strawberry Highball. A homemade strawberry shrub brings a punch of tart sweetness but, Kamholz says, don't stop there. "You’re welcome to mingle with other spirits and other fruits" in this highly modifiable highball recipe.

ba-south-slope.method_text:
1. Combine all the ingredients into your cocktail shaker
2. Shake with ice
3. Strain into a chilled coupe
ba-south-slope.description: The South Slope was created by Michael Madrusan whilst living in the Brooklyn South Slopes area. Michael is a well known bartender, owner of The Everleigh (Melbourne, AU), author of A Spot at the Bar and was also named one of the most influential by Australian Bartender magazine.The cocktail is reminiscent to the Unusual Negroni - with the addition of an orange liqueur and a touch of lemon juice, turning it into a Unusual Negroni Sour, of sorts.
ba-south-slope.garnish: Garnish with a twist of lemon

ba-southside.method_text:
Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker, shake well with ice, double-strain into chilled cocktail glass.
Note:
If egg white is used shake vigorously.
ba-southside.description: Its origins are subject to speculation. It has been proposed that it gets its name from either the South Side district of the city of Chicago, Illinois, or from the Southside Sportsmen's Club on Long Island.

ba-spaceface-from-young-american.method_text: 1. Muddle 1 lime wedge with 6 mint leaves. Add the remaining ingredients, plus ice, and shake until cold. Strain into the glass over fresh ice and garnish.
ba-spaceface-from-young-american.description: A touch of crème de menthe and large bouquet of mint make this tequila cocktail from Chicago's Young American extra-refreshing.

ba-spaghetti-western.method_text:
1. Add ingredients and cubed ice to a mixing glass.
3. Stir for 30-45 seconds.
4. Strain into a lowball glass over a clear ice cube.
5. Garnish with grapefruit twist.
ba-spaghetti-western.description: The Spaghetti Western is a tequila-based cocktail recipe that was created in 2011 by Jessica Gonzalez at Death & Company in New York City, New York. This variation was adapted from the book Mezcal + Tequila Cocktails: Mixed Drinks for the Golden Age of Agave by Robert Simonson.

ba-spanish-monk.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and dry-shake.
2. Add ice, then shake again.
3. Strain into a coupe.
ba-spanish-monk.description: First published in 1951 in Charles H. Baker Jr.’s The South American Gentleman’s Companion, the Spanish Monk combines gin, lemon, green Chartreuse, simple syrup and an egg white. Nick Flower learned the recipe at New York’s Little Branch, and he now serves the classic at his bar Too Soon in Portland, Oregon.

ingredients.name: Orange juice
ingredients.note: chilled, plus orange slices for garnishing

ba-spiced-cranberry-orange-punch.method_text:
1. Heat the water, sugar, ginger, rosemary sprig, cinnamon stick, and star anise in large saucepan over medium heat, stirring often, until sugar has dissolved, about 5 minutes; do not boil. Stir in cranberries and cook, stirring often, until cranberries just begin to pop open, about 3 minutes. Off heat, let cranberry mixture cool completely, about 30 minutes. Transfer to bowl or storage container, cover, and refrigerate until well chilled, at least 1 hour or up to 4 days.
2. Combine the cranberry mixture, seltzer, cranberry juice, and orange juice in large punch bowl. Add an ice ring and garnish with rosemary sprigs and orange slices. Serve in chilled punch cups.
NOTEAn ice ring does the best job of keeping the punch chilled for several hours without overdiluting. If necessary, 8 large ice cubes can be used instead.
ba-spiced-cranberry-orange-punch.description: For a festive spirit-free option to present at holiday parties, stir up this spiced cranberry-orange punch from Cocktails Illustrated by America's Test Kitchen. Spicy ginger, warm baking spices, the herbaceousness of rosemary, and sparkling seltzer elevate this mix of cranberry and orange juices.

ba-spindrift.method_text: 3 ounces orange juice 2 ounces fresh lemon juice 1 ounce passion fruit syrup 3/4 ounce sugar syrup 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract 2 ounces dark jamaican rum 1 1/2 ounces demerara rum 1 ounce light rum 20 ounces crushed ice Put everything in a blender. Blend for up to 10 seconds. Pour unstrained into a large snifter.
ba-spindrift.description: In 2005 the Spindrift was put on the menu of the Taboo Cove bar, at the Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas. Two months later Taboo Cove closed. We don’t know if the Spindrift was directly responsible, but there’s no denying that the drink takes a lot of time to make.

ba-split-decision.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker tin
2. Add ice and shake for 10-15 seconds
3. Strain into a glass with large format ice
4. Express an orange peel
ba-split-decision.description: A delicious cocktail built on a split base of scotch and apple brandy, with Madagascar vanilla and Aperol. It’s warm, balanced, and thoughtfully composed.

ba-squeaky-wheel.method_text:
1. Stir all the ingredients together in a mixing tin with ice, then strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
2. Express the oils of the orange peel over the top of the drink and use as a garnish.
ba-squeaky-wheel.description: "The squeaky wheel gets the oil", my father always used to tell me. This cocktail demands that level of attention, says Nicholas Bennett of Cedric’s at the Shed of this Mezcal Negroni. "I enjoy the combination of coffee and bitters, and I will occasionally add a touch of Angostura to my coffee in the morning, so the blend of St. George NOLA Coffee Liqueur and Campari was almost a no-brainer when I was developing this Negroni variation. The splash of amaretto really rounds out the cocktail."

ingredients.name: Irish whiskey
ingredients.note: preferably Powers Gold Label Irish Whiskey

ba-st-john-frizells-irish-coffee.method_text:
1. Add the whiskey and simple syrup into a mixing tin.
2. Add a small amount of boiling water to an 11-ounce mug to heat it, and nestle the tin in the mug so that the tin heats as well.
3. Dump the water out of the mug, add the whiskey-sugar mixture and top with boiling water to about 1 inch below the rim of the glass.
4. Pour the espresso shot directly into the mug.
5. Float the cream on top and garnish with freshly grated cinnamon.


 ## Editors note:

### Whipped Heavy Cream:

Pour several ounces of heavy cream into a mixing tin. Dry shake without ice until the cream begins to thicken, but is still pourable.
ba-st-john-frizells-irish-coffee.description: The best Irish Coffee cocktail recipe, which won our tasting of variations on the drink, combines Irish whiskey, espresso and whipped cream.

ba-st-regis-julep.method_text: 1. Add all the ingredients to the julep tin and muddle the mint gently with barspoon. Add 2 cubes of cracked ice, stirring to chill. Add crushed ice to fill halfway; let chill. Add more to fill. Garnish.
ba-st-regis-julep.description: "The St. Regis Julep was created by the famous John Swago of the old St. Regis in New Orleans. It is one of the first drinks I ever made from Famous New Orleans Drinks and How to Mix 'Em by Stanley Clisby Arthur," says Cure bartender Ryan Gannon. "It is a funky, awesome riff on a julep that I try to make anytime I get a request for a julep."

ba-star.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass and stir for ten seconds
2. Strain into a cocktail glass and garnish
ba-star.description: A humble riff on the famous Manhattan yields excellent fall flavors

ba-step-into-liquid.method_text: Stir with ice, strain into an old fashioned glass with a large ice cube, and garnish with orange oil from a twist.
ba-step-into-liquid.description: Two Wednesdays ago, I returned the online recipe flashcards for the Liholiho Yacht Club in San Francisco that I utilized for the Pineapple Dance, and I landed on the Step into Liquid. As for a time estimate, I was able to spot the drink on a 2019 menu on Yelp, and it was perhaps named after the 2003 surfing documentary. While I have had other pineapple rum-Campari drinks in the Negroni ballpark, like the Pineapple Kingston Negroni, Best Fronds, and Jungle Boulevard, they all called for regular sweet vermouth instead of Punt e Mes. Once prepared, the Step into Liquid offered up orange, dark rum, pineapple, and herbal aromas to the nose. Next, grape and caramel notes on the sip gave way to rum, pineapple, bitter orange, and herbal flavors on the swallow.

ba-stones-throw.method_text:
1. Add all the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake to chill and strain into the glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-stones-throw.description: What started as a thoughtful exercise about balance, turned into one of the favorite cocktails at Juniper and Ivy in San Diego. "I wanted something bright, grounded, herbal but refreshing, a cocktail that felt like it belonged in the roaring '20s—whether in a dimly lit bar or on a sun-drenched patio," says drink creator and bar lead Alex Siegelin.

ba-stork-club.method_text:
1. Combine all of the ingredients in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.
ba-stork-club.description:
There is a number of cocktails, that came from various New York bars and clubs, which later became classics. Stork Club is one of those venues, that was known for its drinks, back in the day. However, some of those recipes slowly fell into obscurity, just like its signature Stork Club cocktail.

Base of the cocktail is London dry gin with its signature juniper notes supplemented by the gentle citrus and coriander undertones. Triple Sec adds sweet orange flavour, which is later reinforced by the healthy addition of fresh orange juice. A touch of lime juice brings some refreshing tartness to the mix, helping to bring back a little balance and give this cocktail a little pep in its step. Last, but not least a dash of Angostura bitters provides an extra kick of complexity while at the same time seasoning the cocktail.

All in all, Stork Club is a simple cocktail with a slightly unusual balance, due to mellow orange juice, but do not let that fool you, it is tasty – a true delight, especially for orange lovers. Even though it might be a little strange to our modern palate, it is a delicious way to travel back in time.

ba-strawberry-daiquiri.method_text:
1. Use a muddler to crush 2 strawberries in a shaker
2. Add the remaining ingredients and shake well with ice
3. Double strain into a chilled glass
ba-strawberry-daiquiri.description: Dry sherry brings dimension to this update on the strawberry Daiquiri in this recipe from Sweet Liberty Drinks & Supply Co. in Miami.
ba-strawberry-daiquiri.garnish: Skewered strawberry half dusted with black pepper

ingredients.name: Green Chartreuse
ingredients.note: The Silver Dollar suggests Brucato Chaparral or green Chartreuse

ba-strawberry-roan.method_text:
1. Add the first 4 ingredients to a shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain into an ice-filled glass and top with strawberry soda.
3. Garnish.
ba-strawberry-roan.description: “Strawberries and herbs are a classic flavor pair, shown here in a slightly different way,” says Brian Downing, the owner, operator, and lead bartender of Louisville whiskey bar The Silver Dollar. The sweet, juicy notes of strawberry soda balance well with the spice of rye whiskey in this playful highball named for a Marty Robbins song. “I wanted something crushable to enjoy out on our patio, and this hits the spot."

ba-strictly-business.method_text:
1. Add all of the ingredients to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake to chill and strain over fresh ice in a glass.
3. Garnish.
ba-strictly-business.description: The Gold Rush, a modern classic created by Milk & Honey's T.J. Siegal and the late Sasha Petraske, serves as the foundation for this rye whiskey cocktail at Polite Provisions. "When developing this menu, we specifically pulled inspiration from those who had the greatest influence on our cocktail program to date, and many of the teachings of Sasha Petraske hold strong," says Alicia Perry, beverage director for CH Projects. In this twist, rye steps in for bourbon, and oloroso sherry, sweet vermouth, and herbed bitters follow, creating a "fresh qualities, pleasantly herbed, rich and impactful, with a clean, nuanced honeysuckle finish," Perry adds.

ba-strukani-pelin.method_text:
1. A lemon slice is then squeezed directly into the glass and mixed.

The amount of lemon juice can vary, sometimes resulting in a drink with equal amounts of both ingredients. More elaborate versions often add orange juice, citrus zest, or spices.
ba-strukani-pelin.description: Štrukani pelinkovac (or štrukani pelin) is a somewhat novel Croatian drink that combines pelinkovac (traditional herbal liqueur) with lemon juice. In its basic form, the drink is made with pelinkovac that is poured into an ice-filled glass.

ba-sunflower-cocktail-recipe.method_text:
1. In a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients
2. Shake with ice for 10-12 seconds
3. Double strain into an absinthe-rinsed, chilled coupe
ba-sunflower-cocktail-recipe.description: The Sunflower is a creation of well known bartender Sam Ross. A simple variation on the classic Corpse Reviver #2 - substituting Elderflower liqueur in place of the original Lillet or Cocchi Americano.Sam Ross is known for creating numerous modern classic cocktails such as the Penicillin, Paper Plane and the Too Soon?

ba-surfer-on-acid.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker and shake with ice.
2. Strain into a double rocks glass over a large block of ice.
3. Garnish with freshly grated nutmeg.
ba-surfer-on-acid.description: The Surfer on Acid is an easy shaken cocktail recipe made with rum, Jägermeister, lime, pineapple and saline solution.

ba-t-summer-night.method_text:
1. Cut your lime ready for squeeze and garnish and get your mint leaves and mint sprig
2. Fill your wine glass with cubed ice
3. Smash the mint in your hand and put it in the glass
4. Pour your gin, elderflower liqueur, and lime juice over the ice
5. Using your bar spoon, stir all the ingredients together well
6. Add more ice if needed and fill up with prosecco
7. Top up with soda
8. Stir gently and garnish with lime and mint sprig
ba-t-summer-night.description: A special twist on the Hugo cocktail by Tjuvholmen. This breezy sparkling elderflower cocktail will take you straight to Italy in the summertime. And it couldn’t be easier to make. Bartender Tip:Add gin and mint for this special twist

ba-tango-nuevo.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients except the garnishes in a mixing glass and stir briefly, 10-20 seconds
2. Strain into a rocks glass over one large rock
3. Sprinkle a bit of salt on top and garnish with lemon twist
ba-tango-nuevo.description: An offbeat little drink with a confectionary angle
ba-tango-nuevo.garnish:
pinch smoked sea salt for garnish

lemon twist for garnish

ba-tea-time.method_text:
1. Add all ingredients, except ginger beer, to a shaker tin
2. Add ice and shake for 10-15 seconds
3. Strain over ice and top with ginger beer
ba-tea-time.description: Fruity, spicy, and tea-infused elements converge to create a truly unique and delicious non-alcoholic cocktail!

ba-telekinesis.method_text:
1. Combine all ingredients with ice and stir
2. Strain into a cocktail glass, serve up
3. Garnish with one big basil leaf
ba-telekinesis.description: Our in-house version of a tequila Negroni
ba-telekinesis.garnish: basil leaf or orange peel for garnish

ba-temperance-grapefruit-collins.method_text: Add ice to your shaker and shake until it develops a frost.  Double-strain contents (by pouring the contents from the shaker through a fine mesh strainer) into your Collins glass over ice and top with club soda.
ba-temperance-grapefruit-collins.description: The Temperance Grapefruit Collins is an extremely refreshing spirit-free interpretation of the gin-based cocktail of the same name.  As its star ingredient, the grapefruit serves as both the visual and flavor focal point of this simple cocktail.  In the absence of any alcohol, this combination of grapefruit juice, lime juice, and simple syrup is reminiscent of flavors found in the Paloma.  Similarly, as the name suggests, the Temperance Grapefruit Collins is served “tall” in the traditional Collins glass over ice cubes or clear ice spear and topped generously with club soda to give it some fizz.  When it comes to this cocktails preparation, I recommend shaking to both chill and incorporate ingredients; however, to avoid unnecessary explosions, be sure to refrain from adding club soda into the shaker and instead add directly to glassware.  Don’t forget to garnish your Temperance Grapefruit Collins with (you guessed it) a half-wheel of grapefruit.  But don’t take my word for it, make one and try it yourself!
ba-temperance-grapefruit-collins.garnish: Garnish with a half-wheel of grapefruit.

ba-tequila-daisy.method_text:
1. To prepare a coupe or cocktail glass, rim the edge with sugar.
